translations.text: All wisdom comes from the Lord and is with him forever.
The sand of the sea, the drops of water, and the days of eternity: who can count them?
The height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, and the depths of wisdom: who has searched them out?
Before all these things wisdom was created, and the knowledge of understanding from eternity.
To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed, and who has understood the wisdom of her knowledge?
There is one who is wise and greatly to be feared, who sits upon the thrones of his glory.
The Lord created her; he saw her and numbered her, and poured her out upon all his works.
He gave her to all flesh according to his gift, and distributed her to those who love him.
The fear of the Lord is glory and pride, and a crown of joy and gladness.
The fear of the Lord delights the heart and gives joy and grace and length of days.
It will go well with whoever fears the Lord, and after the days of his end he will be blessed.
And the beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord; she was created with the faithful in the womb.
She made her nest among men as an eternal foundation, and mercy was made trustworthy toward their descendants.
The fear of the Lord is the fullness of wisdom, and she makes them drunk with her fruits.
She fills her whole house with desirable things, and her storehouses with her fruits.
The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and it makes the gladness of life blossom.
When he saw her and numbered her, he rained down on her mercy and the knowledge of understanding, and he exalted the glory of those who love his commandments.
The root of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and her branches lengthen the days of life.
A man who is angry without cause cannot be justified, for the scale of anger [?]
A patient man should endure until the right time, and in the end joy is given to him.
For a time he keeps his word hidden in their heart, and many lips will proclaim the praise of his knowledge.
The proverbs of knowledge are among the treasures of wisdom, but godliness is contemptible in the eyes of the ungodly.
If your heart has desired wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord will give her to you.
For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction, and what pleases him is faith and meekness.
My son, do not disobey the fear of the Lord, and do not come to him with a divided heart.
And do not be double-hearted before people, and keep watch over your lips.

Do not exalt yourself, so that you do not fall, and do not bring disgrace on yourself. Otherwise the Lord will reveal your hidden things and cast you down in the midst of the assembly, because you did not come to the fear of the Lord, and your heart is full of deceit.
My son, if you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for every trial.
Let your heart be upright, and endure, and do not be hasty at the time when trial comes upon you.
Draw near to the Lord and do not depart from him, so that you may be exalted at your end.
Endure everything that comes upon you, and be patient in the pains of your humiliation.
For gold is tested by fire, and so too are acceptable people [?] in the furnace of humiliation.
Believe in him, and he will receive you. Order your ways and hope in him.
You who fear the Lord, wait for his mercies, and do not turn aside, so that you do not fall.
You who fear the Lord, believe in him, so that your reward will not fail you.
You who fear the Lord, hope for good things, for mercy and for joy, because the gift of the Lord is eternal and his reward comes with joy.
Look at the generations of old and consider: who believed in God and was put to shame? Or who remained in the fear of him and was forsaken by him?
For the Lord is merciful and compassionate, patient and very merciful. He forgives sins and saves in the time of trouble.
Woe to stubborn hearts and to the slack hands of the sinful man who walks on two paths!
Woe to faint hearts, because they did not believe! For this reason they will not prosper.
Woe to you who have lost your endurance! What then will you do when the Lord calls you to account?
You who fear the Lord, obey his words; you who love him, keep his ways.
You who fear the Lord, seek what pleases him; you who love him, be filled with his law.
You who fear the Lord, prepare your ways and humble your souls before him, and say:
"We have fallen into the hands of the Lord, for his mercy is as great as his riches."
Children, listen to me, your father, and do as I say, so that you may live.
For the Lord has given the father honour over the children and has confirmed the mother's right over her sons.
Whoever honours his father will find forgiveness of sins.
And whoever gives honour to his mother is like one who stores up treasure.
And whoever honours his father will have joy from his own children, and on the day he prays the Lord will hear him.
Whoever honours his father will live a long life. Whoever obeys the Lord will give rest to his mother,
and he will serve his father and mother as he would serve the Lord.
Honour your father in word and in deed, so that his blessing may come upon you.
For a father's blessing makes the houses of his children firm, but a mother's curse tears them up, foundations and all.
Do not take pride in your father's disgrace. For that is not so much a disgrace to you as a glory [?].
For a man's glory comes from honouring his own father, and a father who is not honoured is a reproach to his children.
Child, help your father in his old age, and do not grieve him as long as he lives.
And if his mind fails, forgive him, and do not dishonour him while you have all your strength.
Child, do not forget the kindness of your father, so that it may be built up for you in place of sins.
And in the day of your trouble it will be remembered for you. As ice melts in the warmth from a cloud [?], so your sins will melt away.
For whoever abandons his father is like a blasphemer, and whoever angers his mother's heart is cursed by the Lord.
My son, do your work quietly, and you will be loved by a man whom others accept.
The greater you are, the more you should humble yourself, so that you may find favour before the Lord.
For many who were exalted are brought low, but He reveals hidden things to the quiet.
For the power of the Lord is great. The Lord is glorified by the humble.
Do not search into what is too deep for you, and do not inquire into what is too strong for you.
Think about what has been commanded to you, for you have no need of hidden counsels.
Do not search into matters beyond your concern, which are not needed, for you have already been shown more than human understanding can grasp.
For their own conjecture has led many astray, and evil conjecture has misled the thoughts of the learned.
Whoever loves evil will perish in it.
A wicked heart will come to evil in the end.
A hard heart will be weighed down with pains, and the sinner will heap sin upon sin.
There is no healing for the heart of the proud, for the will toward wickedness has taken root in them.
An understanding heart will grasp a parable, and a quiet and obedient person [?] has a longing for wisdom.
Water puts out a blazing fire, and acts of mercy bring forgiveness of sins.
Whoever repays a kindness will meet it in later times, and on the day of his fall he will find someone to support him.
My son, do not take away the poor man's living, and do not dry up [?] the eyes of the needy with [?].
Do not grieve a hungry soul, and do not anger a man in his destitution.
Do not trouble a grieving heart, and do not put off giving to the needy.
Do not ignore a servant who is in distress, and do not turn your face away from the poor.
Do not turn your eye away from the one who asks something of you, and do not give him cause to curse you.
When he curses you from the bitterness of his heart, his Creator will quickly hear his prayer.
Make yourself loved by the assembly, and humble yourself before rulers.
Lend your ear to the poor, and answer him with a word of peace and gentleness.
Rescue the one who is wronged from the hands of those who wrong him, and do not let his judgment be grievous to your soul.
Be like a father to orphans, and like a husband to their mother. Then you will be like a son of the Most High, and he will love you more than your own mother does.
Wisdom has exalted her children, and she is a helper to those who seek her.
Whoever loves her loves life, and those who rise early for her will be filled with every good thing.
Whoever holds fast to her will hold fast to glory, and wherever he enters, the Lord will bless him.
Those who serve her serve the holy ones, and the Lord loves those who love her.
Whoever listens to her will judge the nations, and whoever pays attention to her will live in confidence.
If he trusts her, he will inherit her with confidence, and his descendants will hold her as an inheritance.
If anyone comes to her with a crooked heart, she will rebuke him from the very beginning. She will send fear and trembling upon him, torment him with her discipline, and test him by her ordinances.
Then she will turn back to him with her mercy, make him glad, and reveal her hidden things to him.
If he goes astray, she will abandon him and hand him over to his own fall.
Keep her commandments, guard yourself against evil, and do not be ashamed for the sake of your soul.
For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that brings glory and joy.
Do not show partiality to the harm of your soul, so that you are not put to shame when you fall.
Do not hold back a word in the time of life,
for wisdom is known through speech, and the knowledge of understanding through the words of the tongue.
Do not speak against the truth in any matter, and do not be put to shame because of your lack of learning.
Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not fight against a strong current.
And do not subject yourself to a foolish man, and do not show partiality to the mighty.
Fight for the truth even to death, and the Lord God will fight for you.
Do not be hasty with your tongue while being sluggish and slack in your deeds.
Do not be like a lion in your house, and do not be fault-finding toward your household.
Do not let your hand be stretched out to receive but drawn back when it comes to giving.
Do not set your heart on your wealth, and do not be weighed down by it. And do not say: “This is enough for me.”
Do not follow your own strength so as to walk after the desires of your heart.
Do not be presumptuous because of your wealth, and do not trust in yourself. And do not say: “Who can prevail over me?” For the Lord will surely take vengeance on you.
Do not say: “I sinned, and now what shall I do?” For the Lord is long-suffering.
Do not be so confident of his forgiveness that you add sin upon sin.
Do not say: “His mercy is great; even if my sins are many, he will wipe them away.” For mercy comes from him, but his anger rests upon sinners.

Do not delay to turn to the Lord, and do not put off drawing near to him from day to day, lest the wrath of the Lord come forth suddenly, and while you delay it crush you, and in the time of vengeance destroy you.
Do not trust in the wealth of falsehood, for it will not profit you in the day of wrath.
Do not winnow with every wind, and do not walk in every path of falsehood, like the sinner and the double-tongued.
Be steadfast in your speech and in your counsel, and let your counsel be one.
Be quick to listen, and patient in giving an answer.
If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; if not, put your hand over your mouth.
For glory and dishonor lie in the power of speech, and a man's tongue is his downfall.
Never let yourself be called a whisperer [?], and do not stumble with your tongue; for shame falls on the thief, but great disgrace falls on the double-tongued.

Do not be ignorant in great matters or in small, and do not become an enemy instead of a friend; for the one with an evil name inherits shame and disgrace, and so does the sinful and double-tongued man.
Do not exalt yourself in the counsel of your soul,
lest you devour your leaves and destroy your fruit, and leave yourself like a dry tree.
An evil soul will destroy the one who has it, and makes him a laughingstock to his enemies.
A sweetly speaking voice multiplies the giving of praise.
Let your friends be many, but let your counsellor be one out of a thousand.
If you find a friend in a time of trouble, test him, and do not trust him at once.
For there is a friend for a season, but [?] he will not stand by you in the time of trouble.
And there is a friend who turns into an enemy and in a quarrel reveals what can be held against you.
And there is a friend who only shares your table, and he will not stand by you in the time of your trouble.
When things go well for you he becomes like your equal [?], and he is harsher with your servants than you are.
If trouble comes upon you, he will turn against you and hide himself from your face.
Keep far away from your enemies, and be on your guard with your friends.
A faithful friend is a strong tower, and whoever finds one has found a great treasure.
A faithful friend has no price, and nothing can match his excellence.
A faithful friend is a medicine of life, and those who fear the Lord will find one.
For the one who fears the Lord, friendship will prosper, for as he is, so is his friend.
My son, choose instruction from your youth, and you will find wisdom until old age.
Like a man who rises early to plough and sow, so approach her and wait for her good fruits, so that you may labour a little in her work and soon enjoy her fruits.
How hard she seems to the uninstructed! Stubborn hearts will not stay with her.
She will rest on such a person like a heavy testing stone [?], and he will not delay in throwing her off.
For wisdom is true to her own [name?], and she is not revealed to many.
Listen, my son, keep my teaching, and do not turn away from my instruction.
Make your feet ready for her fetters.
Put your shoulders under her and carry her, and do not be weary of her bonds [?].
Approach her with all your heart, and keep her ways with all your strength.
Search and seek, and she will be made known to you; and when you have taken hold of her, do not let her go.
Then at last you will find her rest, and she will be turned into joy for you.
Her fetters will become a strong shelter for you, and her chain a golden ornament; you will put her on as a robe of glory.
For her golden ornament is in her, and her bonds are an ornament of conscience [?] and of [?].
You will put her on as a robe of glory, and set her on your head as a crown of praise.
If you want the teaching of wisdom, my son, you will find it.
And if you love obedience, you will come to love it. If you incline your ear, you will be wise.
Stand among the wise elders, and join yourself to the wisest of them.
Be willing to hear every divine word, and do not let the proverbs of knowledge slip away from you.
If you see a man of understanding, go to him early in the morning, and let your feet wear down the thresholds of his door.
Think about the ordinances of the Lord, and meditate on his commandments always. He will make your heart firm and give you the desire for wisdom.
Do no evil, so that harm will not come upon you.
Keep away from falsehood, and it will keep away from you.
My son, do not sow in the furrows of falsehood, so that you do not reap sevenfold harm from it.
Do not ask the Lord for a position of leadership, or the king for seats of honour.
Do not justify yourself before the king, and do not show off your wisdom before his majesty.
Do not seek to be a judge, in case you cannot tell the false from the true, and in case you are afraid before the face of the rich and put a stumbling block in the way of your integrity.
Do not sin against the people of the city, and do not throw yourself into their tumult.
Do not join with two sinners, for you will not be justified even for one of them.
Do not say this: 'He will look on me because of my many gifts; when I make an offering to God Most High, he will accept what I offer.'
Do not lose heart in your worship, and do not neglect to show mercy.
Do not laugh at a man who is humbled and bitter in heart, for the Lord humbles, and he is also the one who exalts.
Do not plot a lie against your brother, and do not do the same to a friend.
Do not wish to tell any lie at all, for the persistence of it [?] is not good.
Do not babble among many elders, and do not make void the words of your vows.
Do not be envious [?] of hard work or of farming, which God created.
Do not count yourself among the many sinners. Remember that wrath does not delay and hell gives no one more time.
Humble yourself, for the punishment of sinners is fire and the worm.
Do not exchange your friend for a bribe, nor a true brother for the gold of Ophir.
Do not part from a wise and good woman, for her grace is better than gold.
Do not mistreat a servant who works faithfully, and do not wrong [?] a hired laborer who has given himself to you.
Let your soul love a sensible servant, and do not deprive him of his freedom.
If you have cattle, look after them; if they are useful to you, keep them.
If you have sons, discipline them, and bend their necks from their youth.
If you have daughters, keep watch over them, do not pamper them, and do not show them a cheerful face.
Give your daughter in marriage, and you will have accomplished a great deed; and give her to a sensible husband.
If you have a wife who is after your own heart, do not cast her out; but if she is hateful to you, do not trust yourself to her.
Honor your father with all your heart, and do not forget the birth pains of your mother.
Remember that you were born through them, and without them you could not have existed. Repay them for what they have given you.
Fear the Lord with all your heart, and honor his priests.
Love your Maker with all your strength, and do not despise his ministers.
Fear the Lord and honor the priest, and give him his portion, as you have been commanded: the firstfruits [?], the offering for repentance, and the sacrifice of holy things.
And stretch out your hand to the poor, so that your blessing may be complete.
Let the grace of your giving extend to all the living, and do not withhold kindness even from the dead.
Do not deprive the dead of your tears, and mourn with those who mourn.
Do not hesitate to visit the sick, for this will make you loved.
In all that you do, remember your end, and you will never sin.
Do not quarrel with a powerful man, lest you fall into his hands.
Do not set yourself against someone stronger than you, lest he outweigh you with gold; for gold has destroyed many and has turned the hearts even of kings.
Do not argue with a talkative man, and do not heap wood on his fire.
Do not jest with a fool, lest your ancestors be insulted.
Do not reproach a man who has turned away from his sins. Remember that we are all under wrath.
Do not insult a man in his old age, for you too will grow old.
Do not take delight in the dead, for you too will die.
Do not despise the word of the wise and their proverbs; let your soul be occupied with them, for from them you will learn understanding and the service of the great.
Do not neglect the teaching of the elders, for they too learned the proverb from their holy fathers. And from them you will learn understanding, and at the time of [?] (need) how to give an answer,
so that you may not be burned by the flame of his fire.
Do not stand up against the face of an insolent man, lest he lie in wait to trip you before your face.
Do not lend to one stronger than you; if you lend, count it as lost.
Do not stand surety for one stronger than you; if you do stand surety, be ready to pay then and there.
Do not go to law against a judge, lest he judge you according to his own eminence.
Do not travel on the road with a reckless man, [?] lest he lay every evil heavily upon you. He will act according to his own will, and you too will perish through his folly.
Do not quarrel with a hot-tempered man, and do not go with him into the desert, for blood is a small thing in his eyes, and where there is no helper, there he will strike you down.
Do not take counsel with a fool, for he cannot keep a word to himself.
Do not do a secret thing before strangers, for you do not know what will come of it.
Do not open your heart to every man, and let no one thank you in vain.
Do not [?] (estrange / be jealous of) the wife of your bosom, lest through you she learn a crooked mind.
Do not give yourself over to women, so that they gain mastery over all your strength.
Do not gaze at the face of a harlot, lest you fall into her snares.
Do not keep company with a [?] (singing-woman / ensnaring woman), lest she catch you with her deceit.
Do not gaze at the beauty of a virgin, lest her comeliness become a stumbling block to you.
Do not give yourself over to harlots, lest you lose your inheritance.
Do not look around in the streets of the city, and do not go astray after their feet [?].
Turn your eye away from a beautiful woman, and do not gaze at another's beauty, for many have been led astray by the beauty of women, and from it love blazes up like fire.
Do not sit at all with a married woman, and do not [?] (feast) with her drinking wine, lest your heart turn toward her and you of your own accord slip into destruction.
Do not forsake an old friend, for a new one will not be equal to him. A new friend is new wine; but when it grows old, you will drink it [?] freely.
Do not envy the glory of sinners, for you do not know the end of their overthrow.
Do not take part in the good pleasure of the ungodly; remember that until Hades you will not be justified.

Keep far from a man who has power to kill, and you will not be gripped by the fear of death. And if you do come near him, do not offend him, so that he does not take your life. Know this: you are walking in the midst of snares, and you are walking upon the [?] of the city's battlements.
Weigh your own strength, and as far as you are able, deal rightly with your neighbor. Let your counsel be with the wise,
and your speech with the intelligent, and let all your discourse be in the law of the Most High.
Let righteous men share your bread, and let your boast be in the law of the Lord.
A work made by the hand of a craftsman is praised; so also the leader of the people who is wise is praised for his word.
A talkative man appears fearsome among his neighbors, and one who is hasty with his tongue becomes hated.
A wise judge will instruct his people, and the rule of the intelligent is well ordered and firmly established.
For as the judge of the people is, so are his servants; and as the leader of the city is, so are those who dwell in it.
An uninstructed king will ruin his people, and cities are built up by the understanding of the rich.
In the hands of the Lord is dominion over the earth, and he raises up the one who is needed at the proper time.
In the hands of the Lord is success, and he sets majesty upon the face of the one who writes.
Do not hold a grudge against your neighbor for every offense, and do not do any deed that comes from hatred,
for the arrogance of men is hateful before the Lord, and from both sides offense is found through falsehood.
Kingship passes from one generation to another because of willfulness and greed.
Why are earth and ashes proud? For even while he lives, his entrails are full of worms.
A physician cuts short a lingering [?] sickness, but a king is here today and tomorrow he will die.
When a man dies, his flesh is inherited by creeping things, beasts and worms.
The beginning of arrogance is a man's falling away from God, and his heart turns away from his Creator.
And the beginning of sin is arrogance, and whoever guards against it will keep far from abomination. Therefore the Lord made his wrath mighty against them and overthrew them completely.
He cast down the thrones of arrogant rulers and seated the meek in their place.
The Lord plucked up the roots of the nations and planted the lowly in their place.
The Lord overthrew the lands of the nations and destroyed them down to the foundations of the earth.
He wiped them out and destroyed them, and made their memory vanish from the earth.
Arrogance was not created along with man, nor furious anger along with those born of women.

An honored race of men: which race is honored? The race of those who fear the Lord. A dishonored race: which race is dishonored? The race of dishonored men who transgress the commandments of the Lord.
Among brothers, their leader is the most honored of them. So too are those who fear the Lord in his eyes.
And their boast is the fear of the Lord.
It is not right to insult a poor man who is wise, and it is not fitting to honor a man who is a sinner and rich.
The rich man, the mighty man and the ruler are glorified, yet none of them is greater than the one who fears the Lord.
Free men will serve a wise servant, and so will his own master's people, and a wise man does not grumble.
Do not think too highly of yourself in your work, and do not glorify yourself in the time of hardship.
For it is better to be one who works with his own hand and lacks nothing at all than one who glorifies himself and lacks bread.
My son, glorify yourself with quiet humility, and give yourself as much honor as you deserve.
Who will justify one who sins against himself? Or who will honor one who disgraces his own life?
The poor man is honored for his understanding, and the rich man for his wealth.
The one who is honored in his poverty is many times richer than the rich man. And the one who is disgraced in his wealth is many times worse off than the poor man.
The wisdom of a humble man lifts up his head and seats him among the rich.
Do not praise a man for his good looks, and do not despise a man for his appearance.
The bee is small among flying creatures, yet what it produces is the chief of sweet things.
Do not boast in the beauty of fine clothes, and do not exalt yourself on the day of your glory. For the works of the Lord are wonderful, and his works are hidden from people.
Many rulers have been brought down [?] to the ground, and one nobody expected has put on the crown.
Many mighty men have been greatly disgraced, and the honored have been handed over into the hands of others.
Do not blame a man before you have examined the matter. First understand, and only then rebuke.
Do not answer before you have listened, and do not get involved in words of rivalry.
Do not quarrel over a matter that does not concern you, and do not rise early to take part in the judgment of the ungodly.
My son, do not rush into many undertakings. If you take on too many, you will never come out blameless. If you chase after them, you will not catch up, and if you run away, you will not escape.
There is one who labors, struggles and hurries, and yet is all the more in want.

And there is one who is weak and sick and has no one to help him. He is short of means and full of poverty. Then suddenly the eye of the Lord looked upon him in his goodness and raised him up from his low state.
He lifted up his head, and the man became a source of wonder to many.
Good and evil, life and death, come from God.
The gift of the Lord remains upon the righteous, and his good favors will prosper forever.
There is one who grows rich by being careful and steadfast, and this is the portion of his reward.
When he says, "I have found rest, and now I will eat and enjoy my goods," he does not know what time will come upon him. He will die and leave it to others.
Stand firm in your covenant, my son, grow old in it, and be careful in your works.
Do not love the work of the ungodly. Trust in the Lord and keep at your works, for in the eyes of the Lord it is easy and plain to make a poor man rich.
The blessing of the Lord is the reward of his servants, and in a swift hour he pours out blessing like a flower.
Do not say, "What do I need now? From now on, what more good can come to me?"
Do not say, "This is enough for me. Why should I toil any longer?"
In the good days remember the evil days, and in the evil days do not forget the good ones.
Does he not know that on the day of the end it is easy in the eyes of the Lord to repay people according to their deeds?
One hour of affliction makes a person forget delight, and at a person's end his deeds are revealed.
Do not call anyone blessed before his end, for a person is known even by his offspring.
Do not bring every person into your house, for the snares of the devil are many.
Like a decoy partridge set in its cage, the heart of the proud is set to deceive, and like a watchman it watches for your fall,
for it lies in wait to turn your good into evil, and it will lay a blemish on your virtue.
From a spark of fire the coals multiply, and a sinful man lies in wait for blood.
Beware of the wicked man, for he contrives evil. Otherwise he may give you over to reproach forever.
If you take a stranger into your home, he will twist you in the day of dismay and make you a stranger to your own household.
If you do good, know for whom you are doing it, so that the favor of your good deed may be found.
Do good to one who serves God and you will find a reward, if not from him, then from God.
One who is quick to evil will find good nowhere. And whoever stretches out his hand to give to the needy —
Give to the one who does good, and do not lift your hand for the sinner.
Do good to the lowly, and do not give to the ungodly. Hold back your bread and do not give it to him, so that you do not meet with twice the evil in return for all the good you did him.
For the Most High also hates sinners and repays the ungodly what they deserve.
Do not set your eyes on sinners,
For a friend is not recognized in good times, and an enemy is not hidden in bad times.
When a man is prospering, his enemies are grieved, and when he is in trouble, even his friends move far away from him.
Never trust an enemy, for his wickedness is like bronze that corrodes.
And even if he grows old and walks bent over, be on your guard and keep yourself safe from him. Be to him like a man who polishes a mirror, and know that it will not stay corroded forever.

Do not set him up firmly beside you, or he may at some point overthrow you and take your inheritance. Do not seat him at your right hand, or he may try to take your rightful seat from you. In the end you will remember these words of mine and regret ignoring my commandments.
Who will pity a snake charmer if a snake bites him, or anyone who puts out their hands and touches the mouth of a wild beast?
In the same way, whoever keeps company with a sinful man becomes a partner in his sins.
Such a man will stumble along with you for a while, but if you turn aside, he will not put up with it.

An enemy speaks sweetly to you with his lips, but in his heart he plots to throw you into a pit. An enemy will force tears from his eyes, but if he finds the chance, he will never have enough of your blood.
If any trouble comes upon you, you will find him there first, and he will set a trap of deceit for you while pretending to help.
He will shake his head and clap his hands. He will whisper a great deal and change the look on his face.
Whoever touches pitch will have his hands smeared with it, and whoever keeps company with an arrogant man will become like him.

Do not lift anything heavier than you can carry, and do not associate with someone richer and more powerful than you. How can a clay pot be a match for a kettle? The one will strike against it, and the other will be smashed by it.
A rich man does wrong and still has his say, but a poor man is wronged by the rich man and must still plead with him.
If he has any need, he will count on you.
If you have anything, he will share your living with you. If you run short, he will abandon you. When he knows that he has now drained you dry, he will leave you, and it will not trouble him at all.
He wanted to, and he has led you astray. He will smile at you and comfort you, and speak kindly to you, and say to you: "What do you need?"

He will lead you astray and shame you with his food until he has drained you two or three times. In the end he will mock you. And afterward, when he sees you, he will drop you and shake his head at you.
Be careful not to be fooled by him, or you will be brought low by your own foolishness.
When a powerful man invites you, keep away from him. The more he calls you, the further you should stay from him.
Do not push yourself forward, or he will push you away. But do not stand too far off either, or he will forget you.
Do not trust his many words, for he will test you with his many words. He will smile as he speaks to you and question you.
Merciless is the one who does not keep a friend's words, and he will not spare you the hardships of his bonds.
Be firm and be very careful, for you are walking alongside your own downfall.
Every animal loves its own kind, and every man loves his equal.
All flesh gathers together kind by kind, and a man will cling to one like himself.
What fellowship has a wolf with a lamb? No more has a sinner with a godly man.
What peace is there between a hyena and a dog? And what peace is there between the rich and the poor?
The wild ass in the desert is prey for lions; so too the poor are food for the rich.
The proud man loathes the humble; so too the rich man loathes the poor.
When a rich man is shaken, he is held up. When a poor man is shaken, his acquaintances push him away.

When a rich man goes wrong, many help him; even if he says something improper, they justify him. When a poor man goes wrong, everyone angrily rebukes him [?]. Even if he says something wise, they do not let him speak.
The rich man speaks, and everyone falls silent and they praise his words to the clouds. The poor man speaks, and everyone scorns him; if he stumbles, they even push him down.
Wealth is good in its own power, and poverty is evil in the sight of the ungodly.
A person's heart changes the look of their face, either toward good or toward evil.
The sign of a good heart is a cheerful face, and coming up with proverbs takes hard thinking.
Blessed is the man who has not slipped with his tongue and has not been stung by doubt over sin.
Blessed is the man who is not pleased with himself and who has not fallen away from his hope.
Wealth does not suit a petty man, and what does a grudging man know about the value of money?
Whoever scrapes together his own portion is gathering for others.
If someone is mean to himself, how will he be good to anyone else? He will never enjoy his own fruit.
Nothing is worse than a man who begrudges himself, and this is the reward of his wickedness.
If he does any good, he does it by forgetfulness, and in the end he shows his wickedness.
Evil is he who looks with envy. He sins with his eye and turns souls aside.
The eye of a greedy man is not satisfied with its portion, and the falsehood of wickedness withers souls.
An evil eye begrudges bread at the table, and it becomes stingy [?] and angry at the tables.
My son, while you are able, do good to yourself and offer worthy sacrifices to the Lord.
Remember that death does not delay, and Hades grants no time.
Before you die, do good to your friend, and help him with your own hand as much as you can.
Do not deprive your days of good, and do not let your share of what you desire pass you by.
so that you do not leave your labour to strangers, nor your portion to be divided by lot.
Before your death, do righteousness. Give, receive, and keep your soul holy, for in Hades there is no seeking of luxury.
All flesh wears out like a garment, for the decree from the beginning is that one shall surely die.
Like leaves sprouting on a leafy tree, where some fall off and others grow, so is the generation of all flesh: some are born and some die.
Every perishable work comes to an end, and the one who did it perishes along with it.
Blessed is the man who meditates on wisdom and speaks with the reasoning of understanding.
Whoever ponders her thoughts in his own heart will understand her hidden things.
Go out and follow her like a tracker, and watch her paths.
He peers in and looks through her window, and is obedient at her doors.
He lodges close to her tent
and stays in that good dwelling.
He will place his children in her shade and will dwell under her branches.
He will be shaded under her shelter from the heat and will abide under her glory.
Those who fear the Lord will do this, and those who are trained in his law will take hold of her.
She will come to meet them like a mother, and like a [?] wife she will receive him.
She will feed him the bread of wisdom and give him the wine of understanding to drink.
He will lean on her and not give way; he will trust in her and not be put to shame.
She will exalt him above his neighbours, and she will open his mouth in the midst of the people.
She will fill him with the spirit of counsel and clothe him in the ornament of glory, and she will set the crown of wisdom and joy on his head. And she will make him inherit an everlasting name.
Foolish men will never reach her, and lawless men will not see her.
They will keep her far from arrogance, and lying men will not remember her.
Praise is not fitting in the mouth of a sinner, for it was not sent from the Lord.
For praise dwells in wisdom, and the Lord himself makes it prosper.
Do not say, 'I fell away because of the Lord'; for I did not do what he hates.
Nor should you say, 'He led me astray'; for he has no need of sinful men.
The Lord has hated every abomination, and those who fear him do not love it.
He himself created man in the beginning and left him in the hand of his own will.
If you wish, you will keep his commandments, and you will keep faith in what pleases him.
He has set fire and water before you; stretch out your hand to whichever you wish.
Death and life are set before a person. Whatever someone loves will be given to them.
For the might of the Lord is great; he is strong in power and sees all things.
His eyes are on those who fear him, and he himself knows what people do.
He commanded no one to be ungodly, and he gave no one leave to sin.
Do not long for a crowd of worthless offspring, and do not rejoice over ungodly children.
Even if they multiply, do not rejoice over them, especially if they do not have the fear of the Lord.

Do not trust in their life and do not rely on their place, for they will groan in untimely mourning. One righteous person who does the will of God is better than ten thousand lawless ones. Count even dying childless as better than having [?] children who do not serve God.
For through one person of understanding cities are built up, but the families of the ungodly are laid waste.
My eye has seen many such things, and my ear has heard even greater ones.
Fire blazed up against the assembly of sinners, and wrath flared up against the lawless people.
For he did not spare the race of the giants of [?bones; perhaps 'ancient'], who rebelled in their might.
He did not spare the place where Lot lived as a stranger, whose people he made abhorrent because of their arrogance.

He did not spare the race of the Canaanites from destruction, and he wiped them out for their sins. He did all this to that stiff-necked people because of their sins, but he did not drive away [?] the multitude of the holy ones. For they had not kept his commandments in the wilderness.
In the same way he crushed the assembly of seventy myriads [700,000] for their hardness of heart.
For if even one stiff-necked person were found anywhere, it would be a wonder if he escaped. For mercy and wrath both come from him. He is mighty to forgive, and also to pour out wrath.
As great as his mercy is, so many times over does his [?forgiveness/reproof] reach. A person will be judged by what he has done.
The sinner will not escape with his plunder, nor will the sinner be [?helped] by his patience.
Everyone will gain a place through mercy, and each person will be found according to his deeds.
Do not say this: “I will hide from the Lord, and who on high will remember me? Who will know me among so many people? What am I among so many people and in a creation beyond measure?”
Look: the heaven of heavens and all the depths lie open to his searching. The high mountains and the foundations of the earth will shake together.
When he looks at them, they quake in terror.
And no one will ponder these things in his heart, and no one will reckon out his ways so as to understand them by his own design. And what he does, how will anyone see it?
For many are his works that are done in secret.
The works of his righteousness, who has proclaimed them, and who is able to? For the covenant with him is far off.
How can one who lacks heart understand? For a foolish man, erring in mind, thinks falsehood.
My son, listen and learn my instruction, and let your ear heed my words.
I will set out in due measure the knowledge of the Lord's creation and of the works from the beginning.
When he created them, he appointed to each one his portion.
He arranged his works in beauty in the world, and his dominion from generation to generation of them. They did not hunger, nor did they grow weak, nor did any one of them cease from his labor.
No one oppressed his neighbor, and they will never transgress the commands of his words.
And then the Lord looked down from heaven to the earth and filled them with his good things.
With the souls of all living creatures he filled its face, and to it he made their return.
The Lord created man from the earth and afterward turned him back to it again.
He gave them a number of days and a measure of times, and made them rulers over them.
As much as they could bear, so much strength he put into them, and he created him in his own likeness.
He laid dread and fear upon all flesh, and gave him dominion over beasts and birds;
a heart of knowledge, eyes and ears he gave them;
he filled them with wisdom and knowledge, and showed them good and evil.
He set eyes in their heart, so that he might show them the riches of his works.
And they would sing praise to the name of his holiness, so that they might tell of the riches of his works and praise him by the name of his holiness.
He added to them the instruction of his knowledge and gave them the law of his life as an inheritance.
And he established an eternal covenant with them.
Their eyes saw the wonder of his glory, and their ears heard the glory of his voice.
He said to them, "Guard yourselves from all wickedness." And he gave each of them commands concerning his neighbor.
Their ways are always before him and are not hidden from his face.
Over each of them, according to their order, he appointed prophets, but he chose Israel as his own portion.
All his works are like the sun before him, and his eyes see all his ways.
Their lies were not hidden from him, and all their sins are before him.
A person's almsgiving is like a signet ring with him, and he will guard a person's kindness like the pupil of the eye.
After this he will rise up and pay them their reward; he will pay it back on their own heads.
But for those who repent he made wide the way back through their repentance, and he comforted those who were failing.
Turn to the Lord and give up sin. Pray before him and cut down your sin.
Make your remembrance to the Most High and turn away from falsehood. Utterly hate what is abominable.
Who will praise the Most High in Hades in place of the living, who give thanks to him?
For from the dead, as from one who does not exist, thanksgiving has perished. The living and those who are alive praise the Lord.
For great is the mercy of the Lord. Those who turn back will find forgiveness through repentance.
For it cannot be that all things should be of use to human beings, for the offspring of humans is not immortal.
What is brighter than the sun? Yet even it fails. And the thoughts of blood and flesh are evil.
He alone knows how to measure the power of the height of heaven, but all people are earth and ashes.
He who lives forever created all things.
And the Lord alone will be shown to be just in all things.
He has made it easy for no one to tell of his works; or who has searched out his works?
And who is able to count up the might of his works? Or who has the power to tell of his mercy?
For nothing can be taken away or added, and no one can search out his wonders.
For when a person has grown weary telling of his wonders, and when he leaves off, then he will be amazed.
What is a human being, and what is his use? What is his good, and what is his evil?
The number of a person's days, if it is great, is a hundred years.
And even these are like a drop of the sea and like a single grain of sand; that is how much those years are compared with the numbers of eternity.
Therefore the Lord was patient with them and poured out his mercies on them.
He saw and understood their ruin, that it is evil. Therefore he multiplied his forgiveness.
For a person's mercy is toward his own neighbour, but the Lord's mercy is on all flesh. He rebukes, teaches and instructs, and brings them back, as a shepherd does his flock.
He has mercy on those who accept his instruction and on those who hasten to his judgments, for the judgment is his.
My son, do not mix reproach with your good deeds, nor grief caused by words with any gift.
Does not the dew relieve the heat? In the same way a word brings more gladness than a gift.
Look, is not a good word better than a good gift? Both of these are found with a gracious man.
A fool reproaches without grace, and the gift of the envious makes the eyes melt.
Learn before you speak, and before you fall ill, take care to get healing.
Before you stand before the seats of the judges, examine yourself, and in the hour of your examination you will find relief.
Before trouble has come upon you, humble yourself, and in the time of your sin turn to repentance.
Let nothing hinder you from fulfilling your vows at the proper time, and do not delay fulfilling them until the time of death.
Before you make a vow, take care to fulfill it, and do not be like a man who puts God to the test.
Remember the wrath on the day of anger, and the time of his vengeance, when he turns away his face.
Remember the time of hunger in the time of plenty, and poverty and want in the times of wealth.
From morning until evening the time changes, and all things pass swiftly before the eyes of the Lord.
A wise man is submissive in all things, and in the days of his sin he guards himself against sin.
Every man of understanding comprehends wisdom, and whoever finds it gives praise to it.
Those who understand the words of rulers become wise and pour out many proverbs of truth.
Do not follow after your desires, and keep your tongue from vain talk.
If you give your soul the pleasure of its desires, you will make yourself something for your enemies to gloat over.
Do not take delight in much luxury, and do not bind yourself by [its] schemes.
Do not bring about your own downfall through [?] and [?], even if [?] something lies in your purse.
A drunken laborer will not become rich. Whoever despises the poor will himself come to want.
Wine and women lead men of understanding out of their right minds, and whoever joins himself to harlots lives shamelessly.
Rot and worms will devour him, and the souls of the shameless will be destroyed.
Whoever trusts too quickly is small of heart, and whoever sins harms his own soul.
Whoever rejoices in his own wickedness will be condemned.
And whoever hates evil talk will lessen wickedness.
Never be fond of repeating a word, and good will never fail you.
Whether with friend or enemy, do not wish to [?] a word. Even if there is no sin on your part, never reveal it.
For he has heard you and will be wary of you, and in time he will come to hate you.
Have you heard something said? Let it die with you. Do not be afraid, for it will not split you open and burst out.
Before speaking, a fool groans, as a woman is in pain before a child at her giving birth,
and as an arrow is lodged in a man's limb, so is a word in the heart of the soul.
Question your friend: perhaps he did not do it; and if he did do it, question him so that he will not do it again.
Question your friend: perhaps he did not say it; and if he did say it, question him so that he will not [?] it again.
Question him, for slander is common, and do not believe every word yourself.
For there is slipping, and not by one's own intent. And who is there who has not sinned with his tongue?
Question your friend before you become angry, and give place to the law of the Most High.
All wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and in all wisdom is the doing of the law.
Teaching of evil is not wisdom, nor are the counsels of sinners wise.
There is not [?] a wickedness that is abominable among them, and they are foolish and lacking in wisdom.
Better is one lacking in understanding who fears the Lord than one full of shrewdness who transgresses the law.
There is an exact knowledge, and it is full of violence and falsehood. And there is one who corrupts favor in order to make a judgment come out.
There is a wickedness that goes about stooped in mourning, and its insides are full of wickedness. There is one with head hung low in black, and his inner self is full of guile.
He covers his face and acts as if he were deaf, and where you do not expect it, there he will rise up against you.
And even if the weakness of his strength keeps him from sinning, if he finds the right time for his wickedness, he will hurry to seize you [?].
A man is known by his eye, and a sensible person is recognized when you meet him face to face.
A man's attire, the laughter of his lips, and the way he walks tell about him.
There is a reproof that is not good, and there is a silence by which one is found to be wise.
For it is much better to reprove than to be angry.
And whoever confesses it is kept from loss.
The desire of a eunuch is to rob virgins of their virginity. So is the one who passes judgment by force.
There is one who is found wise because of his silence, and there is one who becomes hated because of his many words.
And there is a silence like that of one who has no word in his mouth, and there are silent people who know the right time to speak.
A wise man keeps silent until the right time, but the ungodly man lets the time pass.
Whoever multiplies words becomes hated, and whoever is excessively harsh becomes despised.
A man may have success in evil things, and there is gain and there is loss.
And there is a gift that is of no profit to you, and there is also a gift that profits twice over.
And there is loss that comes for the sake of glory, and there are those who lift up their heads out of humility.
There are those who buy much for little, and then pay for it sevenfold.
Whoever is wise in words makes himself loved, but the favors of fools are put to shame.
The gift of the foolish is of no profit, for his eyes expect many things in return for one.
He gives little and reproaches much, and he opens his mouth like a herald. Today he lends, and tomorrow he demands it back. Such a man becomes hated.
The fool speaks like this: "I have no friend, and there is no gratitude for my good deeds."
"Those who eat my bread insult me with their tongues." How often, and by how many, will he be made a laughingstock!
Better to stumble with the foot than with the tongue. In the same way the fall of the wicked will come quickly.
An ungrateful man is like an ill-timed story. Both are always ready [?] in the mouth of the uninstructed.
Proverbs become despised in the mouth of a fool, because he does not speak them at the proper time.
There is one who is kept from sinning by weakness, and when he is at rest he feels no remorse.
And there is one who ruins himself through shame and perishes through his partiality.
There is one who, out of shame, makes a promise to a friend and gains him as an enemy for nothing.
A lie is an evil stain on a man, yet it is always ready [?] in the mouth of the uninstructed.
A thief is better [?] than someone who is accustomed to lying, but both will inherit destruction.
The way of a lying man is a disgrace to himself, and his shame will rise up [?] against him. Words of proverbs:
Whoever is wise advances himself by his words, and a prudent man pleases the rich.
Whoever works the land will raise high his heap of grain, and whoever pleases the rich will find forgiveness for offenses.
Gifts and bribes blind the eyes of the wise, and like a [?] (literally "venom-making") of the mouth they turn back words.
Hidden wisdom and an unseen treasure: what profit is there in either of them?
Better is a man who hides his folly than a man who hides his wisdom.
My child, if you have sinned, do not do it again, but pray all the more about the sins you have already committed.

Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent. If you come near it, it will bite you. The [?] (teeth?) of sin are like the [?] (teeth?) of a lion: they [?], they strike, and they destroy the souls of men.
All lawlessness is like a two-edged sword, and there is no healing for its wound.
[?] (literally "speaking") and insult lay waste to wealth; in the same way the houses of the proud will be laid waste.
The prayer of a poor man is as near to God as the ears are to the mouth, and his judgment comes quickly.
Hatred of reproof is found in the way of sinners, but whoever fears the Lord will turn back in his heart.
The man who is mighty with his tongue is known from far off, but whoever is sensible in his tongue knows his own slip beforehand.
Whoever builds his house with other people's money is like someone who gathers stones into a heap.
The assembly of the lawless is gathered tow, and their end is like a flame of fire.
The ways of sinners are made smooth and cleared of stones, but their end is the pit of hell.
Whoever keeps the law will attain its understanding and its fulfillment. The fear of the Lord is wisdom.
A man who is not wise will not be taught. But what multiplies bitterness is not knowledge.
The understanding of the wise is like a mighty flood, and the counsels of knowledge are like a river flowing from a spring.
The mind of a fool is like a broken clay jar, and it cannot hold any knowledge.
When a sensible man hears a word of wisdom, he praises it and makes it his own. When a pleasure-loving man hears it, he does not like it; he turns his face away and throws it behind his back.
The talk of a foolish man is like a burden lying on the road, but grace is found on the lips of the wise.
The mouth of a wise man will be esteemed in the assembly, and people will ponder his words in their hearts.
Wisdom is like a ruined house to a fool, and the knowledge of his soul is talk without examination.
Instruction is like fetters on the hands to the senseless, like manacles on the right hand.
A fool raises his voice when he laughs, but a man of knowledge smiles quietly and gently.
Instruction is like a gold ornament to a sensible man, like [?] on the right hand.
A fool's foot hurries into a house, but an experienced man is ashamed before people's faces.
A foolish man grows restless and peers toward the house, but a well-taught man stands outside and waits.
It is a man's foolishness to peer in at the door; but whoever is sensible finds such disgrace heavy to bear.
And the lips of strangers [?] stand weighed in the balance.
Their blow [?] is in the mouth of the soul, but as for the wise, their mouth is their heart.
When the ungodly man curses the devil, he does not know this: that he is cursing himself.
The whisperer defiles himself and becomes hateful throughout his whole dwelling place.
The sluggard is cast down like a filthy stone; everyone hisses at him and marvels at his disgrace.
The sluggard is smeared with dung; everyone who touches him shakes off his hands.
Uninstructed children are a shame to their father, and a soul [?daughter] born is a loss.
A sensible daughter is an inheritance for her husband, but the one who causes worry is a shame to her father and mother.
A brazen woman shames both father and husband, and becomes hateful to both of them.
Merrymaking in a time of mourning is like the telling of untimely words, but instruction and teaching are wisdom at all times.
Whoever teaches a fool is like someone sewing together a potsherd, and like someone waking a sleeper from deep sleep.
Whoever tells something to a madman tells it to someone dozing, and at the end he will say, "What are you saying?"

Weep for the dead, for he has lost the light; and weep for the madman, for he has lost his understanding. Weep only a little for the dead, for he has found rest, but the life of the fool is worse than death.
Mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but for the madman and the fool all the days of his life are cause for mourning.

Do not multiply words with a foolish man, and do not walk on the road with him. Beware of him, so that he does not wear you out or defile you. When he shakes himself off, turn away from him and you will find rest, and his shamelessness will not become a grief to you.
What could be heavier than [?] the wise man, or what other name does it have except "madman"?
Salt and sand and a lump of iron are easier to carry than [?] a foolish man.
Just as a well-built house [?] is not destroyed in an earthquake, so too a heart established on sensible counsel will not give way in a time of crisis.
A heart established on wise counsel is like all kinds of ornaments set with beads on a plastered wall.
And just as stakes set up on a high place are shaken by the wind, so too a sluggish heart set on mad counsels cannot hold out against any fear.
If anyone strikes the eye, tears pour out; and whoever angers the heart brings out its true nature.
Whoever shoots at birds drives them away, and whoever reproaches a friend destroys the friendship.
Even if you draw a sword against a friend, do not cut off hope, for there is still a way back.

And if you have opened your mouth against a friend, do not be dismayed [?], for there is also reconciliation. But do not reproach him, do not be arrogant toward him, do not reveal his counsel, and do not strike him with deceit. These are the things that make friends part from one another.
Be faithful to your friend in his poverty, so that you may rejoice with him in his good fortune. In a time of trouble stand by him and trust him, so that you may share in his inheritance with him.
Before the fire comes the flame, and before the furnace the smoke; so also before bloodshed comes strife.
And I will not be ashamed of the reproach, or of sheltering a friend with me, and I will not hide from his face.
And if some harm comes to me because of him, I will not be ashamed of that on his account either. For everyone who hears of it will beware of him.
Who will set a guard over my mouth and a trustworthy seal on my lips, so that I may not fall because of it and my tongue may not destroy me?
O Lord, my Father and God of my life, do not abandon me to their counsels, and do not let me fall by them.
Who will set stern discipline over my thoughts, and the teaching of wisdom over my heart? Then they would not spare my rash errors or forgive my sins,
so that my acts of ignorance may not multiply and my sins may not pile up against me. Otherwise I would be found fallen at the feet of those who hate me, and may my enemies never triumph [?] over me.
O Lord and Father, God of my life, do not abandon me to their counsels, and do not give me over to the haughtiness [?] of my eyes.
And turn desire away from me.
Do not let the cravings of my belly and the desires of impurity overcome me, and do not hand me over to the words of a shameless soul.
Children, listen to this teaching of wisdom. Whoever keeps it will never go astray through his own words.
For by it the arrogant [?], the slanderer and the sinner will be brought down.
Do not let your mouth get used to oaths, and do not get used to swearing by naming the holy ones.
For just as a servant who is constantly examined will not escape bruises, so too the person who constantly swears and invokes the name will not be free from sin.

A man who swears often will be filled with lawlessness, and the scourge will not leave his house. If he sins, his sins remain with him [?]; and if he disregards it, he has sinned twice. And if he swears falsely, he will not be justified, for his house will be filled with retribution.
There are words that are equal to death. Let them not be found in the inheritance of Jacob. For the righteous will flee far [?] from all these things, and they will not be defiled by sins.
Do not let your mouth get used to the sin of lawlessness through lack of discipline, for a word of sin is bound up with it.

Remember your father and your mother, for you sit among the rich. Otherwise you may forget yourself in their presence and become a fool [?] through your habits. Then you will wish and say, "Would that I had not been [?] at once [?]," and you will curse the day of your birth.
A man who gets used to words of reproach will not be disciplined in all the days of his life.
There are two kinds of people who multiply sin, and the third brings wrath.
A hot-tempered soul is like a fire once it has been kindled, and it does not die down until it [?]. A man who commits fornication with his own body of flesh will not stop until death.
A man goes down from his bed and says in his heart: "Now who sees me? Darkness surrounds me and my walls hide me; no one sees me. Whom should I fear now? The Most High will not remember my sin."

His fear is only of the eyes of men, and he does not know that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the shining light. At all times they see the ways of men and behold every hidden secret.
For before anything was yet created, he knew all things, and their end is known to him.
Such a man will be punished in the midst of the cities, and he will be seized there, where he does not expect it.
So also a woman who leaves her husband and produces an heir by a stranger:
first, she has despised the law of God; second, she has sinned against her own husband; third, she has played the harlot in adultery and raised up children by a strange man.
Such a woman will be brought before the judge's seats, and she will be judged and punished together with her offspring.
The roots of her children will not spread, and her branches will not bear fruit.
Her memory will perish from the earth, and her disgrace will never be blotted out.
So those who remain will understand that nothing is better than the fear of the Lord, and nothing is sweeter than it. Do you heed these commandments of his?
Wisdom praises herself and boasts in the midst of her people.
In the churches she will open her mouth, and before her people she boasts of the birth of Christ.
"I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, and like a mist I covered the earth.
I dwelt in the heights, and my throne was on the pillar of cloud.
Alone I went around the edges of the sky over the earth, and I trod the depths of the abyss.
I went about on the waves of the sea and over all the earth, and I gained all the nations.
After all this I sought a resting place. In whose inheritance shall I rest now?
Then the Creator of all things commanded me. He who created me gave me a resting place in his tent and said to me: 'Dwell in Jacob, and let Israel be your dominion.'
He created me from the beginning, before the ages, and I shall never fail.
In his tent I serve before him, and Israel is my dominion.
I took root among a glorious people, in the portion of my inheritance. On the mountain of the Lord I was established in [?] palms.
I grew like a cedar of Lebanon and like a cypress on the mountains of Hermon,
like a palm tree in Engedi [?], like a rose plant in Jericho, like a beautiful olive tree in the plain. I grew tall like a plane tree by the watercourses.
Like cinnamon and blended aspalathus [?], and like choice myrrh, I spread my fragrance. I was like the incense reed, galbanum, onycha and stacte, and like the frankincense burned in the tent.
Like a terebinth I spread out my branches, and my branches are branches of glory and grace.
I, like a beautiful vine, brought forth grace, and my flowers are the fruit of glory and riches. In me is the hope of all living things, with strength.
Come near to me, you whose heart has desired me, and be filled with the produce of my fruit.
For the memory of me is sweeter than honey from the honeycomb. My name is forever, and the memory of me is from generation to generation.
Those who eat of me will want more, and those who drink of me will thirst for me again.
Whoever listens to me will never be put to shame, and those who love me will never sin. Those who make me glad will be saved forever.
All this is the book of the commandments of the Lord, the knowledge of the truth given to us, the law that Moses commanded as an inheritance for the people of Jacob.
It fills wisdom to the brim like the Pishon, and like the Tigris in the days of summer.
It fills with wisdom like the Euphrates, and fills with understanding like the Jordan in the days of harvest.
It makes instruction shine out like light, and like the Gihon in the days of the grape harvest.
The first ones could not reach the beginning of knowledge, and the last ones will not be able to search it out.
For its understanding has grown greater than the sea, and its counsels greater than the great deep.
And I was like a channel from a river and like a stream, when [?] it flows toward paradise.
I said: "I will water my gardens and soak my garden beds [?]." And look, my stream became a great river, and my river became a sea.
Now I will rise early and make my teaching shine like the dawn, so that it may shine far off.
Still more, I will pour out teaching like prophecy. I will leave it to the generations forever.
Now see that I have not toiled for myself alone, but for all who seek it.
I adorned myself with these three things, and with these three I was made beautiful: harmony among brothers, love of a neighbour, and the unity of wife and husband with each other.

These are three kinds of people my soul hated, and I greatly loathed their way of life: a proud poor man and a lying poor man, a lying rich man, and an old man who is foolish and lacking in understanding.
If you did not gain understanding in your youth, who will give you understanding now in your old age?
How beautiful are just judgments among the grey-haired, and among the elders also the understanding of knowledge.
For wisdom is beautiful among the aged.
And their boast is the fear of the Lord.

These nine thoughts are beyond understanding. I have counted them blessed in my heart, and the tenth I will speak with my tongue: a man who rejoices over his children and in his own lifetime sees the downfall of his enemy,
and blessed is he who lives with a sensible wife, and who has not slipped with his tongue.
Blessed is he who has found wisdom and who tells it to ears that listen.
Great is the glory of the one who has found wisdom, yet he is not as great as the one who fears the Lord.
The fear of the Lord has surpassed everything. The one who has gained it, to whom shall he be compared?
Let it be any wound at all, only not the wound of the serpent; let it be any wisdom at all, only not the wickedness of a woman.
Let it be any attack at all, only not the attack of those who hate; let it be any vengeance at all, only not the vengeance of an enemy.
There is no other head greater than the head of the serpent, and there is no other anger greater than the anger of the enemy, and there is no other wickedness greater than the wickedness of a woman.
It is better to share a house with a lion and a dragon than to share a house with a wicked woman.
A woman's wickedness drains the colour from her husband's face, especially when she twists her face and snarls like a bear.
Even if her husband is sitting [?] with his companions, whenever anything is mentioned, her husband sighs.
All wickedness is small compared with the wickedness of a woman. Let it fall to her as the portion of a wife [?], and let her enter the inheritance of the ungodly.
As a sandy slope is to the feet of an old man, so is a sharp-tempered woman to a gentle husband.
Do not be enticed by a woman's beauty. Do not be softened by her long gazing, and do not long for a woman.
For when a woman gives orders to her husband, there is anger, shamelessness, and great disgrace.
A crushed heart, a bowed head, and a wounded heart: such is a woman, a demon in the house. Drooping hands and weakened knees come from a woman who has not called her husband blessed.
Sin had its beginning from a woman, and because of her all die.
Do not let water go out and spread, nor give [?] boldness to a wicked woman.
If she has not learned to follow your hand, cut her off from your flesh and cast her away.
Blessed is the husband of a gracious woman, and the number of the days of his life [?] twofold [?] to his mind [?].
A sensible woman gladdens her husband and fills the years of his life with peace.
A gracious woman is a good portion, and she will be given as a portion to the one who fears the Lord.
Whether he is rich or poor, his heart will be generous, and at all times his face will be cheerful.
My heart was troubled by these three things, and concerning the fourth I prayed: slander in a city against a great multitude of people, and vain [?] are worse than death.
A woman who quarrels with a sensible man brings pain of heart and grief of mind; the lash of the tongue is enough for everyone.
Like a shaking ox-yoke, so is a wicked woman; whoever touches her is like someone who takes hold of a scorpion with his hand.
A drunken woman is a great cause of anger, and she cannot even cover her own shame.
A woman's fornication is exposed by the [?] of her eyes and by the fluttering of her eyelids.
Keep a stricter watch over a shameless daughter, so that she does not find an opportunity and run loose of her own will.
Beware of a woman with a roving eye, and do not be surprised if she sins against you.
Like a thirsty traveller who opens his mouth and drinks any water near at hand, mixed as it is, she attaches herself to every peg and opens her quiver to every arrow.
A woman's charm delights her husband, and her good sense puts fat on his bones.
A gentle woman is a gift from the Lord, and a well-taught daughter is beyond price.
A modest woman is grace upon grace, and nothing is equal to a faithful daughter.
As the sun shines out in the heights of the Lord, so the beauty of a good woman is the ornament of her house.
Like a lamp shining on the holy lampstand is the beauty of a face on a firm [?] figure.
Like golden pillars on a silver base are beautiful feet set at the gates.

Two things grieve my heart, and a third has brought great anger on me: a brave man when he is weakened by poverty; wise men when fools treat them with contempt; and a righteous man who turns back to those same sins after many labours. The Lord has given his people over to the sword.
A merchant will not keep himself free from sin, and a shopkeeper will not save himself from lawlessness.
Many have sinned through negligence, and whoever wants to multiply sins turns his eyes away.
A peg is driven into a cleft in the rock, and between the giving and taking of [?], sin is crushed in [?].
Unless people hold quickly to the fear of the Lord, their houses will soon fall.
When a sieve is shaken, the refuse stays behind. In the same way people are sifted by their own minds when they reason things out.
The furnace tests the potter's vessels, and in the same way the tongue is tested by its reasoning.
As a fruitful tree is known by its fruit, so the words of reasoning [?] a person's heart.
Do not praise a man before he reasons, for this is how a man is tested.
If you pursue righteousness, you will soon reach it and put it on like a glorious robe.
Every bird settles with its own kind, and truth returns to those who practise it.
The lion lies in wait for its prey, and in the same way sin lies in wait for those who do lawless things.
The speech of the righteous is wisdom at all times, but the fool changes like the moon.
Among fools, watch for the right moment, but among thoughtful people, rise early.
The talk of a madman is offensive, and their laughter is sinful indulgence.
The words of a man who swears a lot make your hair stand on end, and their insolence makes people cover their ears with their hands.
Bloodshed comes from the quarrelling of the proud, and their abuse is painful to hear.
Whoever reveals a secret destroys trust and will not find a friend suited to himself.
Love your friend and trust him. If you reveal his secrets, do not look back to him any more.
For as a man destroys his enemy, so you have destroyed the friendship of your neighbour.
Like a bird you have let go from your hands, you cannot bring it back.
Do not chase after him, for he has gone far from you. He has escaped like a gazelle from a snare.
For a wound can be bound up, and after abuse there can be reconciliation. But whoever reveals a secret has cut off hope.
Whoever winks with his eye is plotting evil, and whoever sees it will keep away from him.
To your face the enemy will make his mouth sweet, and he will win your admiration with his words. But in the end he will twist his mouth and twist your words [?].
There are many sins that I have hated, but I have compared none of them to this, and the Lord too has hated them.
Whoever throws a stone straight up will have it fall back on his own head, and a treacherous wound multiplies wounds [?].
Whoever digs a pit for his neighbour will fall into it himself, and whoever sets a trap will be caught in it himself.
Whoever piles up evil against his neighbour will have it roll back onto himself, and he will not know where the evil came from.
Mockery and insolent reproach belong to the proud, and vengeance lies in wait for them like a lion.
Those who rejoice at the fall of the righteous will be caught in a trap, and pain will wear them away until the day they die.
Enmity and anger are also a great abomination, and sinful men are carried away by them.
Whoever seeks retribution will meet it from God, and his sins will be utterly worn away [?].
Forgive your neighbour his offence. Then, when you pray, your sins will be forgiven you.
If a man keeps malice against another man, how then can he ask the Lord for mercy?
If that man has no mercy on someone like himself, how then can he ask forgiveness for his own sins?
He himself is only flesh, yet he knows how to keep up enmity. Who else will show mercy for his sins?
Remember the time of the end and put an end to enmity. Think about death, and quickly hold to the commandments.
Remember the commandments and do not bear enmity toward your neighbour. Think about the covenant of the Most High, and put wickedness away from you.
Keep away from strife, and your sins will become fewer, for the anger of a hot-tempered man stirs up strife.
A sinful man upsets friends and stirs up division among those who live in peace.

The more the fire is fed, the more it flares up; and the more strife increases, the more fighting is stirred up. The stronger a man is, the more his anger grows; and the greater his wealth, the higher his wrath will rise.
A hasty quarrel sheds blood.
If you blow on a spark, you kindle a fire, and if you spit on it, you put it out; and both of these come out of your mouth.
Curse the whisperers and the double-tongued alike, for they have destroyed many who lived in peace.
A slandering [?] tongue has shaken many and driven them out from nation to nation. It has torn down strong cities and overturned the houses of the rich.
A double-speaking tongue has driven out worthy [?] women and deprived them of what they worked for.
Whoever loves such a tongue will not find rest, nor will he dwell in peace.
The blow of a whip makes a wound, but the blow of the tongue breaks bones.
Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not as many as have fallen by the edge of the tongue.
Happy is the one who is sheltered from it, who has not followed its anger, who has not carried its yoke, and who has not been bound with its fetters.
For its yoke is a yoke of iron, and its fetters are of bronze.
The death it brings is an evil death, and even Hades is better than it.
It will not prevail over the godly, and they will not be burned in its fire.
But those who forsake the Lord will fall into its hands; it will blaze up among them and not be put out. It will be sent against them like a lion, and like a leopard it will tear them to pieces.
Be careful and stand firm: fence in your land with thorns, and lock up your silver and your gold.
Make a measure and scales for your words, and put doors and locks on your mouth.
And be careful not to stumble and fall before those who lie in wait for you. Whoever repays a kindness afterward will find deliverance in the time of his fall.
Whoever shows mercy lends to his neighbor, and whoever opens his hands in good faith keeps the commandments.
Lend to your neighbor in his time of need, and in turn repay your neighbor on time.
Keep your word and be faithful to him, and you will always find what you need.
Many have treated a loan as a windfall and have brought trouble on those who lent to them.

Until he has received it, he kisses the lender's hands, and over the other man's goods he changes his voice in all sorts of ways. But when it is time to pay back, he drags out the time, gives him only tiresome words, and at that time cries "woe!"

If he [?] makes an effort, he will barely get back half, and he will count even that as a windfall. If he cannot get it back, then it is as if the borrower had robbed him of everything, and he has made an enemy of him for nothing. The borrower heaps curses and insults on him, and instead of honor repays him with insult.
Many have refused to lend, not out of wickedness, but because they were afraid of losing their money for nothing.
But you, be patient with the poor man, and do not put off showing him mercy.
For the sake of the commandments, be a helper to the poor man and supply what he lacks, and do not send him away empty-handed.
Spend your silver for your brother and your friend, and do not let it rust away among the stones and be lost.
Instead, lay up your treasure as the Most High has commanded you, and it will profit you more than gold.
Store up mercy in your treasury, and it will deliver you from every evil.
Better than a mighty shield and better than a strong spear, it will protect you from the face of the enemy.
A good man stands surety for his neighbour, but one who has lost his shame will leave him stranded in the middle.
Do not forget the kindness of your surety, for he gave himself in your place.
A sinner will overturn the kindness of his surety, and one who is ungrateful in mind will leave his surety to pay.
Standing surety has ruined many who were prosperous and set them tossing like the waves of the sea.
It has driven men from their homes and made them wander among foreign nations.
A sinful man will rush into standing surety, and whoever pursues trading for profit will end up facing judgment for it.
Help your neighbour as far as you are able, and take care of yourself, so that you do not fall.
The first necessities of life are bread and water and clothing, and a house to cover one's nakedness.
Better is the life of a poor man under a roof of beams than all kinds of food from a stranger's table.
Do not measure great and small with your eye,
for it is a bitter life to go from house to house, and wherever you are a stranger you will not find freedom to speak.
You will be grudging [?] and grumble for nothing, and on top of all that you will hear evil words.
