He will say to you: "Go, stranger, and prepare the table for me, and feed me with your own hand."
"Get up, stranger, and go out. Show me the house [?], for my brother is coming to me as a guest, and the house [?]."
These things are hard for a man who has sense: the rebuke [?] of the household and the reproach of the lender.
Whoever loves his son will make up his mind to beat him, so that he may rejoice when the son reaches maturity.
Whoever disciplines his son will gain by him and will boast of him among his friends.
Even if his father dies, it is as though he had not died, for he has left behind one like himself in the world.
In his lifetime he saw his son and rejoiced, and at his death he was not grieved.
He has left behind someone to take vengeance on his enemies and to repay kindness to his friends.
Whoever pampers his son will bind up his wounds, and at every cry his heart will tremble.
An unbroken horse turns out wild, and a son raised without restraint turns out undisciplined.
If you pamper your son, he will astonish you; and if you play with him, he will grieve you.
Do not laugh with him, so that you do not grieve with him and in the end grind your teeth.
Do not give him authority in his youth, and do not overlook the follies [?] of his wickedness.
Bend his sides while he is still a boy, or else he will grow stubborn and disobey you, and be a grief to your heart.
Discipline your son and deal properly with him, so that you too do not go astray through his disgrace.
A poor man who is alive and sound in his body [?] is better than a rich man who is badly afflicted in his body.
Life and good health are better than all fine gold, and bodily life is better than excessive wealth. Concerning foods
No wealth is better than bodily health, and no other joy is greater than joy of heart.
Death is better than a bitter life, and fitting rest is better than prolonged illness.
Good things poured out before a closed mouth are like food set out on a tomb.
It is as much use as an offering laid before idols, for they neither eat nor smell. And that servant receives the wages of lawlessness; so too does the one who is persecuted by the Lord.
He looks with his eyes and sighs, like a eunuch who embraces a virgin and groans.
Do not give your soul over to worry, and do not torment yourself with your thoughts.
Gladness of heart is a man's life, and the joy of his life is a man's length of days.
Cheer yourself, comfort your heart, and put anxiety far from you. For many are those whom worry has destroyed, and nothing is gained by it.
Envy and anger shorten your days, and worry brings old age before its time. A cheerful and generous heart knows how to take care of its food.
Lying awake over wealth wastes away the bones, and the worry it brings drives away sleep.
Anxious wakefulness takes away slumber; a severe illness drives off sleep.
The rich man toils at gathering wealth, and when he rests he is filled with his luxuries.
The poor man toils in the want of his livelihood, and when he rests he becomes needy.
Whoever loves gold will not be justified, and whoever pursues corruption will be filled with it.
Many have been given over to ruin because of gold, and their destruction was right before their faces.
It is a tree of stumbling to those who worship idols beneath it, and every fool will be broken by it.
Blessed is the rich man who has been found blameless and has not gone astray after the track of gold.
Who is he? Let us call him blessed, for he has done wonders among his people.
Who is there who has been tested by it and found perfect? Let him be a cause of pride for us. Who could have gone along with it and did not transgress, and did not commit a sinful deed?
His good things will be made secure with him, and the people will tell of his almsgiving.
If you have sat down at a rich man's table, do not open your mouth wide in gluttony, and do not say in your heart, "There is much on it."
Remember how evil a wicked eye is. What is there among God's creatures more evil than the eye? For this reason it sheds tears more than any face.
Therefore, wherever he looks, do not let your heart be eager [?] to reach into the dish along with him.
Judge your neighbor's feelings by your own, and consider him in every proper way.
Then eat what is set before you as a man should, and do not chew with both [?], so that you do not become hateful.
Be the first to stop, for the sake of good manners, and do not be [?], so that you do not go wrong.
Do not stretch out your hand before they do.
How good a little is for a well-instructed man! And upon his bed [?].
Healthy sleep comes from a moderate belly; he rises early and his mind is with him. The pain of sleeplessness, the trouble of indigestion, and griping of the loins are with the insatiable man.
If you have been forced to overeat among your foods, get up and find relief.
Listen, my son, and do not despise me, and in the end you will find these words of mine true: be diligent in all your deeds, and no sickness will touch you.
Lips will bless the one who is generous with bread, and the testimony to his goodness is trustworthy.
The city murmurs against the one who is stingy with bread, and the testimony to his wickedness is true.
Do not show off your valor over wine, for wine has destroyed many.
As furnaces test the edges of swords in tempering, so wine tests the hearts of the proud in quarreling.
Wine is like life to men, if one drinks it in moderation. What life is there for those who lack wine? For it was created for the joy of men.
Wine is gladness of heart and joy of soul to the one who drinks it in measure.
It is bitterness of soul to the one who drinks it to excess, with rivalry and stumbling.
Drunkenness increases among fools; it lessens strength and adds wound upon wound.

When drinking wine, do not reproach your neighbor over the wine, and do not make him an object of scorn in your merriment. Do not speak a word of reproach to him, and do not distress him by demanding that he repay a loan.
If they make you master of the feast, do not be arrogant, but be among them as one of them. Take care of them first, and only then sit down to eat.
and let every need of yours be met. Only then take your place [?], and by the grace of beauty receive a crown.
Speak, old man, for it is fitting for you, with a steady mind, not with the arrogance of [?].
Where it is a time for listening, do not drag out your anger there, and do not show off your skill in vain.
A chalcedony stone set in a gold ornament: such is a choice company of singers at the drinking of fine wine.
An emerald stone set in a gold setting: such is a sweet voice at the drinking of wine.
Speak, young man, about what you need, when you are asked two or three times.
Keep your speech short. On many matters be very knowledgeable, yet still say nothing.
Do not make yourself an equal among the rich, and where old men are speaking, never chatter.
Lightning hurries ahead of thunder, and grace goes ahead of the modest person.
Get up in good time and do not be the last to leave. Hurry to your home,
and do not be slow about it. Enjoy yourself there and do as you like, but not with sin and not with proud words.
And at every turn bless your Creator, who makes you drunk with his good things.
Whoever fears the Lord will accept instruction, and those who rise early to seek him will find favour.
Those who seek the law will be filled with it, and those who act falsely [?] will stumble over it.
Those who fear the Lord will find justice, and their righteous deeds will shine like lamps.
A sinful man avoids reproof, and he finds a judgment that suits his own will.
A man of understanding does not despise advice from an outsider, but the proud man takes no advice.
Do nothing without first taking counsel, so that you will not be sorry after the deed is done.
Do not walk on the road of stumbling, and then you will not trip on that stony, pathless ground.
Do not trust even the straight road,
and be on your guard even with your own children.
In everything you do, be faithful to your own soul, for this is keeping the commandments.
Whoever is faithful to the law heeds the commandments, and whoever hopes in the Lord will never lack anything good.
No evil will happen to those who fear the Lord, and if they fall into trial, the Lord will rescue them from it.
A wise man will not hate the law, but the deceitful man who deals with it is like a boat in a storm.
An intelligent man believes the law, and the law is trustworthy to him.
Prepare your words, and then they will be heard; set your mind in order, and only then give an answer.
The heart of a fool is like a cartwheel, and his thinking turns around like a cart's axle.
A mocking friend is like a stallion in heat: he neighs under everyone who rides him.
Why is one day better than another, when all the light of the year comes from the sun?
They were set apart by the knowledge of the Lord, and he made seasons into feasts. He separated night from day.
Some of them he exalted, magnified and sanctified, and some of them he placed among the number of ordinary days.
He created man from the earth, and Adam was made from the soil.
God instructed him with much teaching and made their ways different.
Some of them he blessed and exalted, and some of them he sanctified and brought near to himself, and he turned them out of their place. Some of them he cursed and brought low.
As the potter's clay is in his hands, to be shaped as he wishes, so man is in the hands of God his creator, who repays them according to his own judgment.
Good stands opposite evil, and life stands opposite death; in the same way the sinner stands opposite the godly.
So look at all the works of the Most High: they come in pairs, one opposite the other.
I awoke last, and I inherited them as from the beginning. I was like a gleaner following the grape-pickers,
but by the blessing of the Lord I came forward, and like a grape-picker I filled the winepress.
Consider that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who seek wisdom.
Hear me, you rulers of the people, and you leaders of the tribes, give ear [?] to me.
Do not give son or wife, brother or friend, power over yourself as long as you live, and do not give your property to others, so that you will not regret it and end up turning back to them, [?].
While you are still alive and there is breath in you, do not hand yourself over [?] to anyone.
For it is better for your children to ask things of you than for you to look to your children's hands.
Excel in all your works, and do not bring a stain on your honor.
In the days of your end, the days of your life, divide up your inheritance.
Fodder, a stick and a load are for a donkey; bread, discipline and work are for a servant.
And you will find rest. If you leave his hands idle, he will soon ask you for his freedom.
Yoke and strap bend the necks of the proud, and chains and beatings are for a servant who does evil.
Set him to work, as is fitting for him, so that he does not stand idle. For idleness has taught many evils.
And put him to work as befits him. If he does not obey you, increase his punishments, so that he does not become negligent because of his flesh.
And do nothing outside of justice.
If you have one servant, treat him as yourself, for you have acquired him with your own blood.
If you have a servant, treat him as a brother, for you yourself are in need of him.
If you mistreat him, he will get up and run away from you, and you will not find him by any road you search.
The confidence of a foolish man is vain and false, and dreams give wings to fools.
Like someone who would grasp at a shadow and chase the winds is the one who follows dreams and says, “This means something, and that means something.”
The visions of dreams are like a face showing the likeness of a face.
What can be made clean by what is unclean? Or what truth can come from a lie?
Divinations and dreams are vain. Like the pangs of a woman giving birth, they make the mind imagine one thing after another.
If a vision is not sent from the Lord, do not give your heart to it.
For dreams have deceived many, and they have fallen away from their hope.
The law is fulfilled without deceit, and wisdom is made complete in the mouth of those who have knowledge.
A trained man understands everything, and one who has been tested in many things speaks with understanding.
Whoever has not been tested in struggle knows little, but whoever has been trained increases in knowledge.
I have seen many things in my life, and I have more words of understanding about these things than these.
Many times I was in distress to the point of death, and I escaped on these occasions [?].
The spirits of those who fear the Lord will live, for their hope is in their Savior.
Whoever fears the Lord fears nothing else and is not cowardly, for the Lord himself is his hope.
Whoever fears the Lord, blessed is his soul. He looks to no one else; or who is his support?
The eyes of the Lord are on those who fear him. He is their protector and a mighty support of strength, a shade from the heat and a cover at noon, a hope against stumbling and a help against falling.
He lifts up souls and gives light to the eyes. He grants healing, life and blessing.
And sacrifices of falsehood are [?] as an offering, and the Lord will not accept a lawless gift.
The Most High is not pleased with the sacrifices of the ungodly, nor does he forgive sins because of their many offerings.
Like someone who slaughters a son before his father is the one who offers a sacrifice bought with what belongs to the poor.
The life of the poor depends on the bread of their need, and whoever seizes it from them is a man of blood.
Whoever separates husband and wife murders his neighbour, and whoever cuts off a labourer's wages is counted among those who shed blood.
If one person builds and another tears down, what do they gain? Only more toil.
If one person blesses and another curses, whose voice will the Most High hear?
If someone washes after touching a dead body and then touches it again, what has the washing gained him?
So it is with a man who fasts for his sins and then goes and does the same things again. Who will hear his prayer? What has he gained by humbling himself?
Whoever keeps the law multiplies offerings, and whoever heeds the commandments offers a sacrifice of life.
Whoever repays a kindness offers fine wheat flour, and whoever shows mercy offers a sacrifice of praise.
Turning away from evil pleases the Lord, and turning away from falsehood brings forgiveness of sins.
Do not appear before the Lord empty-handed, for all these things are done because of the commandments.
The sacrifice of the righteous enriches the offering, and its sweet fragrance rises before the Most High.
The sacrifice of a righteous man will be accepted, and the memorial of his sacrifice will not be forgotten.
Glorify the Lord generously, and do not hold back the firstfruits of your hands.
Let your face be cheerful whenever you give a gift, and dedicate the tithe with joy.
Give back to the Most High for what he has given you, and give cheerfully whatever your hand has found.
For he is the one who repays, and he will repay you sevenfold.
Do not offer him a bribe, for he will not accept it, and do not set your heart on a sacrifice gained by falsehood,
for the Lord is the judge, and with him there is no favouritism toward human rank.
He shows no one favour at the expense of the poor, and he quickly hears the prayer of the one who has been wronged.
He will not ignore the prayer of the orphan, or of the widow when she pours out her prayers before him.
Do not the widow's tears run down her cheek? And does not their flow fall upon those who made them flow?
Whoever serves with goodwill will be accepted, and his prayer will reach up to the clouds.
The prayer of the humble passes through the clouds, and it will not rest until it arrives
and will not turn back until the Most High looks into it, judges with righteousness, and the Lord himself carries out justice.
And the Most High will not delay, nor will he let them go,
until he has crushed the necks of the merciless and repaid vengeance among the nations;
until vengeance has wiped out the multitude of the arrogant and he has broken the sceptre of power of the wicked;
until he repays each person according to his deeds; according to people's deeds and according to their thoughts he will repay;
until he [?] the judgment of his people and makes them rejoice in his mercy.
For mercy is beautiful in a time of affliction, like a rain cloud in a time of drought.
Have mercy on us, O Lord God of all, and look upon us; spread the fear of you over all the nations.
And raise your hand against all the foreigners, and let them see your might.
As you were glorified in us before them, so be shown mighty among them before us.
And let them know you, as we have known you, for there is no God besides you, O Lord.
Renew wonders and bring back signs; glorify your hand and your right arm.
Rouse your anger and pour out your wrath; destroy the enemy and wipe out the adversary.
Hasten the time and remember the day of judgment, and declare the wonders of your riches.
By the wrath of his fire may the enemy who is not to escape be crushed; and may those who oppressed your people find destruction for their corruption.
Crush the heads of the enemies who said, “There is no one besides us.”
Gather all the race of Jacob.
O Lord, have mercy on your people who are called by your name, Israel, whom you likened to the firstborn.
Have mercy on the city of your holiness, Jerusalem, the place of your rest.
Fill Zion so that it may receive your words,
and raise up prophets for your name's sake.
Give a reward to those who wait patiently for you, and let the prophets prove trustworthy.
Hear, O Lord, the prayer of your servants, according to the blessing of Aaron upon his people,
so that all may understand that you are the Lord God forever.
The belly digests every food, yet one food is better than another.
The palate tests the taste of game, and so a wise heart tests words of understanding and of truth.
A perverse heart will bring grief, but an experienced man will repay him.
Every man will accept a wife, but one woman is better than another.
A woman's goodness makes the face glad, and it surpasses everything a man desires.
If there is mercy and peace on her tongue, her husband is not like other sons of men.
Whoever has gained a sensible wife has begun the acquisition of life: a helper for him and a pillar of rest.
Where there is no fence, the fruit is plundered; and where there is no wife, men groan like wanderers.
For who trusts a lone robber who moves from city to city?
So too is a man who has no nest of his own and lodges wherever night overtakes him.
Every friend will say, "I too am a friend." But there is a friend who is a friend in name only.
And is it not a grief unto death when a companion and friend turn into enemies?
O wicked thought, where did you roll in from to cover the dry land [?] with deceit?
A friend rejoices with his friend, but in the time of trouble he rises up against him.
And there is a friend who toils [?] with you for the sake of his belly, but on the day of battle he does not take up the shield.
Do not forget a friend in your heart, and do not leave him unremembered in your riches.
Every counselor gives counsel, but there is a counselor who counsels only for himself.
Guard yourself against a deceitful counselor, and first find out what he needs, for he counsels for his own sake. Otherwise he may lead you astray in [?] places
and say to you, "That way of yours is good," and then stand opposite you to see what evil [?] befalls you.
Do not take counsel with someone who looks askance at you, and hide your counsel from those who envy you.

Do not consult an ungodly man about piety, or a liar about righteousness, or a faint-hearted [?] man about a contest, or a man from afar about exchanging [?], or a buyer [?] about selling, or an envious man about gratitude, or a merciless man about kindness, or a lazy man about work, or a hired laborer [?] about paying wages, or a stubborn servant about ordering a great deal of work. Do not hold to any of these in any counsel.

Instead, in everything let your counsel be [?] above all with a godly man, one you know from the heart keeps the commandments and whose mind is like your own mind. If you fall, he will grieve for you.
And let the counsel of your heart be with him, for no one is more faithful to you than he is.
For a man's own mind is closer than seven watchmen who sit on the heights to keep watch.
And above all this, pray to the Most High to direct your ways in truth.
The beginning of every work is the word, and counsel is the guide of every deed,
and the place [?] of parables is the heart. For four parts spring up from it:
Good and evil, life and death: and the tongue has power over them.
There is a man who is deeply learned and a teacher of many, yet he is of no use to himself.
And there is a man skilled in words who becomes hateful to everyone, and he is lacking in wisdom;
for grace has not been given to him by the Lord, and he is lacking in all understanding.
There is a wise man who is wise for his own sake, and the fruit of his understanding, coming from his mouth, is trustworthy.
A man of understanding will be filled with blessing, and all who see him will call him blessed.
The life of a man is numbered, but the days of the Lord are without number.
Whoever is wise will inherit glory among his own people, and his name will endure forever.
My son, test yourself during your life, and know what is bad for it, and do not give that to it,
for not everything is good for everyone, and not everything pleases everyone in every way.
Do not be greedy for every luxury, and do not throw yourself on every kind of food,
for pain follows much eating, and gluttony brings on [?] (perhaps colic or nausea).
Many have died through great greed, but whoever guards against it will add to his life.
Honour the physician for his usefulness, for the Lord himself created him too.
For healing comes from the Most High, and the physician receives gifts from kings.
The physician's skill will raise up his name, and he will be honoured in the presence of the rich.
For God created medicines for healing out of the earth, and a man of understanding will not despise them.
Were not the waters made sweet by that wood, so that his power might be made known?
And he himself gave knowledge to people, so that he might be glorified in his wonders.
By it he healed and took away pain. The ointment-makers [?] also mix their ointments with it,
and without these the work can no longer be completed, and through him there is peace on the earth.
My son, do not neglect your sickness, but pray to the Lord and he will heal you.
Put away sin from yourself, and your hands will prosper; cleanse yourself from all sin.
Offer fragrant incense and a wheaten offering [?] as a memorial for yourself; make your sacrifice rich and fragrant.
And make room for the physician too, for God created him as well. Do not let him leave you, for you need him.
And there is a time when you will succeed (be healed) by his hand,
for he too prays to the Lord that he may grant them rest, and healing for their life.
Whoever sins against his Maker, let him fall into the hands of the physician.
My son, let your tears fall over the dead, and like one in great pain begin to lament. Wrap his body as is prescribed, and do not neglect his burial.
Give yourself over [?] to weeping, make your wailing great, and mourn as much as is fitting for him, for one day or two days, to avoid reproach; and then comfort your heart,
for death comes from grief, and the word [?] (sorrow) of the heart bends the heart down from its strength.
Sudden destruction, anxiety, and a life of poverty inflame [?] the heart.
Do not give yourself over to anxiety; put it away from you. Remember the end.
And do not forget that there is no error [?] (return); you will not help him, and you will harm yourself.
Remember his commands, for it will be so for you as well: for me yesterday, and for you today.
When the dead is at rest, his remembrance comes to an end; be a comforter at the departure of his soul.
The wisdom of the scribe comes through the freedom of leisure, and one lacking in understanding cannot become wise by this.
How can a man become wise who holds the plow and boasts in wielding the goad, with the shouting at the oxen, and who rises early for that same work? His thoughts are on the offspring of bulls.
His heart is set on making the furrows straight, and his wakefulness goes into feeding the flocks.

So too the carpenter and the master builder, who spend the night as they do the day. And the one who draws and carves the engravings of seal-stones into an image, and in their wakefulness they set apart the various kinds of workmanship. He gives his heart to the likeness of the drawing, and their wakefulness completes the work.

So too the smith sits near the furnaces and examines the irons. The vapor of the fire melts his flesh, and he struggles against the heat of the flame. The sound of the hammer deafens his ears, and his eyes are on the pattern of his works. He gives his heart to finishing the work, and his wakefulness adorns the work.
So too the potter sits at his work and turns the wheels with his foot. He is always intent with care on his work, and all his works are counted.
With his arm he shapes the clay, and his strength is bent before his feet. He gives his heart wholly to the glazing [?], and his wakefulness to the firing and cleaning of the kiln.
All these trust in their hands, and each one becomes wise in his own work.
Without them a city cannot be built, yet they do not settle down or walk about in it.
But they are not sought out [?] for the council of the people, and the assembly passes over them [?]. They do not sit on the judges' seats, and they cannot understand the law of judgment,
nor can they set forth instruction and justice, and they are not found among the parables. But they establish good works, and their prayer is in the work of their craft.
But he who gives himself into the hands of God and meditates in his thought on the law of God will search out the wisdom of all who went before, and will be occupied with the prophecies.
He will walk in the teaching of renowned men and in the figures of parables.
He will seek out the hidden meanings of parables and will occupy himself with obscure parables.
He will be known before princes and will travel to the land of foreigners and gentiles, for a man has tested good and evil.
He set his heart to rise early to the Lord, his Creator. He will make supplication before the Most High, open his mouth and pray for his sins.
If the Lord God wills, he will fill him with the Holy Spirit. For he himself will pour out to him the word of wisdom, and he will give thanks to the Lord in worship.
He himself will direct his counsel and his knowledge, and he will come to understand his hidden things.
He will make known to him the learning of his teaching, and he will live by the law of the covenant of the Most High.
Everyone will praise his understanding, and it will never be blotted out. His memory will not pass away either, and his name will live from generation to generation.
Nations will tell of his wisdom, and all the people will proclaim his praise.
If he lives on, he will leave behind renown. And if he goes to his rest, it will be better still than before.
Further, I will consider and tell you, for I have been filled like the waning moon.
Listen to me, holy children, and bud forth like a rose, for it is planted beside a stream of waters.
As fragrant incense gives off its fragrance, make your flower blossom like the lily and give off your fragrance. Praise in song and bless the Lord for all his works.
Give him great majesty, and confess his praise in song. Praise God with a voice of praise, and say this as you confess him:
"For the works of the Lord are very good, and every command of his will come about in its time. No one should say, 'What is this?' or 'Why is this?' For everything will be sought out in its time.
At his command the waters stood like a heap, and at the word of his mouth the storehouses of waters.
At his command all his will is done, for there is no one who could diminish it or his salvation.
The works of all flesh are before him, and nothing is hidden from his eyes.
With him there is no lessening and no increasing, and there is no number to his salvation from everlasting to everlasting. He has looked, and nothing is marvelous before his eyes.
No one should say, 'What is this?' Nor should anyone say that this is worse than that. Everything has been created for its own uses and stands firm.
His blessing spread out like a river, and as dry land is drenched by a flood,
so too his wrath will take possession of the gentiles who do not seek him, just as he changed their waters into [?] color.
His ways are straight for the holy, but for the lawless they are a stumbling block.
For good things have been prepared for the good from the beginning; so too, for the sinner, good things are turned into evil.
The basic needs of human life are water, fire, iron, salt, wheat flour, milk and honey, the blood of the grape, and clothing.
All these things are prepared for those who do good, and likewise for evil for those who do evil.
The everlasting winds are prepared for vengeance, and by his wrath their scourges were made strong. At the time of their end they will pour out their strength and calm the anger of their Creator.
Fire and death: all these were prepared for vengeance upon them.
The [?] of lions, scorpions, vipers, and the sword, to take vengeance on the ungodly and destroy them.
They rejoice at his command and are made ready on earth for their uses, and when their time comes they do not go beyond his word.
Therefore from the beginning I was confirmed in this. I thought it over in my mind and set all of it down in writing.
The works of God are all good, and all that he provides is made ready in its own time.
And no one can say, "This is worse than that," for he will make everything fit in its own time.
Now let us bless the name of the Lord with all our heart and mouth.
Great toil was created for humans, and a heavy yoke lies on the children of Adam, from the day they come out of their mother's womb until the day they return to the mother of all.
Their thoughts and the will of their heart are the thoughts of their anxiety until the day of their end.
From the glorious one who sits on the thrones of lordship to the poor one who rolls in earth and ashes,
from the one who is fed with [?] and wears a golden crown to the one who is clothed in coarse cloth, there are wrath, envy, terror, trembling, the fear of death, enmity and strife.
At the time of his searching, the sleep of the night changes his mind.
He rests a little, as if for nothing, and then in a dream, as in the sight of day, his heart is terrified, like one who flees from the face of battle.
And at the time of his battle he wakes up and is amazed that there was nothing to fear.
So it is with all flesh, from humans to beasts, and seven times more on sinners:
death and wrath, blood and sword, captivity and famine, ruin and scourging.
All these are prepared for the lawless, and because of them the flood came upon the world.
Everything that is of the earth returns to the earth, and everything that is of the waters returns there, to the sea.
Every bribe of wickedness will be blotted out, but faith will endure forever.
The wealth of the wicked will dry up like a torrent, and like loud thunder it will turn into rain.
He will rejoice in the opening of his hands, but those who transgress the commandments will likewise perish at the end.
The offspring of the ungodly will not multiply their branches, and the roots of the unclean are on cool rock.
Like [?] that springs up by every water and on the banks of a river, it is plucked before everything else [?].
[?] … by mercy shall endure forever. The life of the self-sufficient [?] is made firm by the work of his hands, and better than both is one who has found wealth.
Having children and building a city make a name last, and more than both of these a blameless wife is valued.
Wine and merriment gladden the heart, and more than both of these is the love of wisdom.
The flute and the harp make a voice sweet, and more than both of them is a sweet tongue.
The heart [?] tells the eye of grace and beauty, and lovelier than both of them is the green growth of what is sown.
A friend and a companion meet each other in due season, but more than these is a wife's meeting with her own husband.
Brothers and help are for a time of trouble, but more than both of these, almsgiving and mercy rescue from trouble.
Gold and silver raise a person very high, but more than both of these, good counsel makes a person pleasing.
Wealth and strength lift up the heart, but more than both of these the fear of the Lord lifts a person up. Those who fear the Lord lack nothing, and they have no need to look for help.
The fear of the Lord is like a paradise of blessing, and it gives more shelter than any glory.
My son, do not live a life of begging, for it is better to die than to beg.

A man who looks to another man's table: his life is not counted among real lives, even if he keeps his eyes fixed on a stranger's food until he is full. A man of understanding and learning guards himself against this.
But to a shameless mouth begging is sweet, and in his belly it burns like a fire.
O death, how bitter the thought of you is to a man who lives in peace among his possessions, a man without cares who prospers and is still able to enjoy pleasure.
O death, your sentence is good for a man who is poor and lacks strength, who is very old, who will not listen to instruction, and who has lost his patience.
Do not shrink from this, O death. Remember those who came before you and those who come after, for they are with you.
This is the sentence from the Lord on all flesh. Why then do you [?] the will of God, whether ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years? In Hades, for the reckoning of human life [?].
My son, the children of sinners are abominable and unclean, and they are caught up in the same ungodly life.
They have lost their patience, and disgrace will grow up along with their descendants.
Children reproach their ungodly father, because they suffer disgrace on his account.
Woe to you, ungodly men, who have abandoned the law of God Most High.
Even if you have children, your offspring will be in need. And if you die, a curse will carry you off.
Everything that comes from the earth will return to the earth, and so the ungodly will go under a curse to destruction.
People mourn over a man's body, but the name of the ungodly will be wiped out because of their wickedness.
Work hard for your good name, for it will stay with you [?] rather than thousands of great treasures of gold.
The days of a good life are numbered in time, but a good name will remain forever.
Keep the instruction of peace, children. Hidden wisdom and an unseen treasure: what profit is there in either of these?
Better is the man who hides his folly than the man who hides his wisdom.
Now, therefore, be ashamed according to these words of mine. For it is not good to keep every kind of shame, and not everything is approved by everyone in faith.
Shame is due before father and mother for fornication; before a ruler and a mighty man for a false word;
before a judge and an official [?] for a sin;
before the assembly and the people for lawlessness; before the place where you live for theft;
before the truth of God, and for the commandments, and for spreading out your hand over the table;
for reproach in asking and in giving at its proper time, and for silence before those who greet you;
for gazing at a woman; for turning your face away from another, from your own kinsman;
for taking a portion and giving it; for looking at the face of a married woman;
for making a pretext of your desire for your maidservant, and do not approach her bed;
before friends, for words of reproach; and for giving after not reproaching [?];
and for obedience in hearing a word [?], and for disclosing secret words.
In all these things be truly modest, and you will find favor with all people.
Child, do not be ashamed of these things, and do not sin out of partiality:
of the law of the Most High and his commandments, and of judgment that justifies the sinner;
of a word of partnership and a shared journey, and of the giving of the inheritance of others;
and of accuracy in [?] and the scales, and of acquiring much by little;
of the giving and taking of merchants, and of much discipline of children, and of making the sides of a wicked servant bleed.
And with a wicked woman, sealing and caution are good; and where the hand is not honest, lock things up;
and whatever you give, give it by number, and receive everything in writing.

Do not be ashamed of instructing the foolish and the mad, and the very old man who is liable to judgment for fornication. Then you will be truly instructed, and you will be found tested and approved by every living being.

A daughter is a hidden sleeplessness to her father, and his thoughts about her drive away his sleep. In her youth he worries that she may pass beyond the age for marriage. When she is married he worries that she may be childless and hated,
and while she is a virgin, that she may become an object of reproach; and when she is with a bridegroom [?], that she may go astray.

Set a watch over a shameless daughter, lest she find a way and go about by her own will, and she make you something trampled underfoot by your enemies and a byword in the city and in the assembly of the people, and put you to shame among many.
Do not gaze at the beauty of every person, and do not [?] among women,
for from the garment itself comes forth the moth, and from the woman herself comes forth wickedness.
Better is the wickedness of a man than the wickedness of a woman: a woman who brings shame to the point of disgrace.
Remember the works of the Lord: what I have seen I will recount to you by the word of his command, his works and all his will in righteousness.
The rising sun shines forth upon all alike, and the works of his [?service] are full of the glory of the Lord.
The Lord did not [?] to his holy ones. Recount all his marvels which the Lord, the [?Almighty], created, to establish all things by his glory.
The deep abysses and the thickness of [?] he devised. The Lord Most High understood all their mind, and he looked upon the everlasting sign,
to recount all that is to be, and to reveal the traces of hidden mysteries.
Nothing passed by him, nor was anything hidden from him; of all thought, not a single word.
The richness of his wisdom adorned him, as he is forever and ever. Nothing is added to him and nothing is lacking, nor was he in need of the counsels of others.
How desirable are all his works, even to a spark to behold!
All this stands and waits forever for every need; it is obedient in all things.
All things are in pairs, one corresponding to the other; he made nothing deficient.
Who has been satisfied with seeing his glory?
The counsel of the height, of the holy firmament, the sight of the heavens, for beholding his majesty.
The sun, when seen, proclaims its rising; the vessel of grace, a marvelous work of the Most High.
At midday it parches the earth; who can stand before its heat?
Furnaces under bellows are a work of heat; it is three times more. The sun scorches the mountains; with mingled fire it breathes out a fierce breath, and its shining blinds the eyes.
Great is the Lord who made it, and by his word he stilled its courses.
And the moon, in all its seasons, serves to show the times, the everlasting times.
From the moon comes the sign of the year; a light that wanes at its end,
for the year is named after it, increasing marvelously in its waning. A vessel of the hosts, it shines forth in the firmament of heaven.
The adornment of the heavens, the glory of the stars, illumined the world from the Lord on high.
And by the holy word they stand in their order and are not released from their prison.
Look at the rainbow and bless the one who made it, for it is beautiful in the splendor of its brightness.
He set the heavens in their place by the circle of his glory; the hands of the Most High stretched them out.
By his command the snow is spread out, and he speeds the lightnings he has prepared.
For this reason the storehouses are opened, and the clouds fly out like winged birds.
By his abundance he gave strength to the clouds, and the hailstones are broken in pieces. The sound of the thunder strikes the earth,
and at his look the mountains shake. By his will the south wind blows,
and the blast of the north stirs up the winds.

Like winged birds he scatters the snow, and it settles like a swarm of locusts settling. As it comes down to the earth, the beauty of its whiteness dazzles [?] the eyes, and the heart marvels at its falling.
He pours the frost over the earth like salt, and when it freezes [?] it becomes like the points of thorns [?].
The cold north wind blows, and ice freezes over the waters and settles on every gathering of them, and it clothes all the waters as if with a breastplate [?].
It devours the mountains, scorches the wilderness and withers the green plants as fire does.
And afterwards that same one, Jesus [?], will plant everything again quickly with healing; a mist covers, and like dew it brings cheer after the heat.
By his counsel he covered the deeps,
those who go down to the sea [tell of its dangers], and we marvel at what our ears hear.
There are his glorious and varied wonderful works, and the various kinds of sea monsters he made.
Because of him its end prospers, and by his command everything is made firm and stands.
However much we say, we cannot reach the end, and after all our words the conclusion fits everything: he himself is all.
Let us glorify him if we are able at all, for he himself is greater than all his works.
The Lord is greatly to be feared, and his power is wonderful.

Raise your voices in the glory of the Lord as much as you have strength, for he is exalted above everything. Increase your praise of him with all your might. Do not grow weary of the labor, for you will not be able to reach the end.
Who has seen him and is able to describe him? Or who can glorify him as he deserves?
Many of his wonderful works are hidden, greater than these, for we have seen only a few of his works.
For the Lord made everything, and he gave wisdom to his servants.
Come, let us praise the famous men, our fathers in our generation.
The glories that the Lord created are many, and their abundance has been from the beginning of their days forever and ever.
Those who held power on the earth used their royal authority to give counsels of wisdom from their hearts, and they declared their prophecies.
They led the people by their wisdom and by the knowledge of their scribal learning; they set the people on the path of the wisdom of words.
The teaching of their delights, the judgment of sweetness in the voice of their fasts [?], to recount the order [of it] in writing.
Rich men, who served with strength and lived at peace in their dwellings,
all of these were glorified in their generation, and in their own days was their boast.
And there are some of them who left something behind in the world so that their praise would be told.
And there are some who have no memorial. They perished as though they had never been, and they became as though they had not existed, and so did their children after them.
These were men of mercy, whose righteous deeds have not been forgotten.
And it remains with their descendants and waits until the end.
And their offspring because of them.
Their descendants will remain forever, and their glory will not be blotted out.
Their bodies were buried in peace, and their name will live forever.
The peoples will tell of their wisdom, and the congregations will speak their praise.
Enoch pleased the Lord and was taken up alive. He was given as an example to many generations.
Noah was found righteous and perfect. In the time of wrath he became a watchman [?] for the world; because of this the flood came.
And an everlasting covenant was made with him, that the flood would not destroy all flesh.
Abraham became the great father of many nations. No one was found like him in glory.
He kept the covenant and the law of the Most High, and he made a pact with him, and in the time of testing he was found faithful.

Therefore he confirmed it to him with an oath: that the nations would be blessed in his descendants, that his descendants would be multiplied and increased like the stars of heaven and like the sand of the sea, and that they would inherit from sea to sea and from the River to the end of the earth.
And through Isaac too he confirmed it in the same way, for the sake of Abraham his father.

To give blessing to all people, the glory and the covenant of their law. And he made it rest on the head of Jacob. He acknowledged him with a blessing, gave him an inheritance, and divided his descendants into twelve tribes.
The man of mercy, who found favour in the sight of all flesh, beloved of God and of all flesh: Moses, whose memory is blessed.
He made him equal in glory to the glories of his glory [?].
By his word, and by signs and wonders, he made him great [?] and glorified him before kings. He gave his commandments to his people and showed them his glory.
Because of his faithfulness, peaceableness and humility, he chose him out of all flesh.

He let them hear his words and drew him into his cloud. And he gave them his commandments face to face, the law of life, with the sign of wisdom, to teach Jacob his law and his judgments to the sons of Israel.
To exalt Aaron, the holy one, who was like him, and his father [?] too, from the tribe of the Levites.

He confirmed the eternal covenant with him and gave him the priesthood of the people. He made him blessed with his adornment, clothed him in the robe of glory and girded him with the belt of perfection.
And he strengthened them with the equipment of strength, with [?] flowing [?], with the long robe [?] and with shoulder-pieces bearing signs [?].

He adorned him all around with the likeness of pomegranates and with many golden bells. He fastened on him the high [?] of his gold, and as he stepped forward its sound [?] was heard in the great temple, as a memorial for the tribes of his people.

The holy robe, woven with gold and blue, a work made with skill and embroidered, on the breastplate of judgment, to correspond to the truth [?], of twisted [?] purple, made by the work of a craftsman.

It was made with precious carbuncles, as engraved work, as work of set gold, with costly and glorious stones as an eternal memorial, with engraved writing according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
With a golden crown upon the adornment of the [?], like the image of the holy seal, to glorify honour, a work of power, a wondrous sight, his beauty before him.
Such things had not existed since the beginning of the world, and no stranger's offspring put it on, but only his sons and his grandsons forever.
On their altars they shall offer it every day, twice, continually.

Moses filled his hands and anointed him with the oil of holiness, him and his descendants until the days of heaven, so that together they might serve him in the priesthood and bless his own people in his holy name.
He chose him out from all the living to offer the sacrifice before the [?] Almighty, with fragrant incense as an eternal memorial, for the forgiveness of the sins of his [?] people.
He gave him the commandment of his holiness, authority over the law and the judgment of righteousness, to teach Jacob his testimonies and to proclaim his judgment upon Israel.
Strangers rose up against him, and men were jealous of him in the wilderness: such as Dathan, such as Abiram, and the band of Korah's camp, in the fury of their wrath.
The Lord saw it and was displeased, and their days were ended by the wrath of his anger. He did a sign and a wonder against them and consumed them with a flame of fire.
And he added to Aaron's glory and gave them an inheritance. He allotted him the fruit of the firstborn and prepared the firstfruits for him in hope.
And they would eat the sacrifice of the Lord, which he gave to him and to his descendants.

But he shall not inherit the land along with his people, and that portion shall not be his among the people; for He himself is his portion and inheritance, and the Lord himself is in the midst of Israel.

Phinehas son of Eleazar was third in glory. Through his zeal, which came from the fear of the Lord, and his firmness in overcoming the people by the courage of his heart, he made forgiveness for Israel.
For this reason his covenant was established: that he would be the leader of the holy ones and of his own people, with the priesthood of abundance forever.
There is also the covenant he made with David son of Jesse, of his tribe, as an inheritance for the people of the king, of the only-begotten son, and as an inheritance for Aaron and his descendants.

Now bless the Lord, who is generous and does good, so that he may give understanding to your hearts and judge his people in righteousness. Then their good things will not become useless, nor their glory among their descendants.

Joshua son of Nun was mighty and a warrior. He succeeded Moses in prophecy. True to his name, he became great in saving, and he was chosen for his courage to take vengeance on the people that rose up, so that he might give Israel its inheritance.
How glorious he was when he stretched out his hands against the cities!
Who has ever stood firm anywhere as he did? For he shepherded all the warriors of the Lord.
By his hand the sun turned back, and one day became as long as two.
He called on God, the Most High and Mighty, when he was pressing and destroying his enemies on every side. God heard him with stones mixed with hail, by the power of the Mighty One,

so that they fell on the nation of the enemies. At his [?descent; text reads "creation"] he crushed the nations of those who attacked, so that the gentiles might understand that their own destruction had come, because their war was before the face of the Lord.

For he followed the Almighty God completely. In the days of Moses he himself did an act of mercy, he and Caleb son of Jephunneh, by standing up to face the opposition and holding back the people from sins, when they were ready to gather [?] because of the matter of their wicked murmuring.
These two alone were saved out of all that great people to bring them into the land of inheritance of the promise, which flowed with milk and honey.
The Lord gave Caleb strength, and it stayed with him until old age, so that he could go up to the high places of the land and reach them. And his descendants held that inheritance,
so that all the children of Israel might see that it is better to follow in the footsteps of the Lord.
Let the judges also know [?] that it is better to walk in the track of his name. Their hearts did not commit fornication, and they did not turn back from the Lord. May his memory be blessed.
May their bones flourish again from their place, and may their names be renewed in the glory of the offspring of their kindred.
Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, was beloved by the Lord. He anointed kings and rulers and set them over the people.
He judged the people by the law of the Lord, and the Lord visited Jacob.
By his faithfulness he proved the prophets true, and by his word he confirmed that their visions were trustworthy.
He called on the Lord every day and at all times because of the distress caused by his enemies, with the sacrifice of an offering of a suckling lamb.
The Lord thundered from heaven; with a great and terrible voice he made his voice heard.
And he crushed the chiefs of Tyre and all the rulers of the Philistines.

And before his rest, at the end of his days, he bore witness before the Lord and his anointed, and said concerning property: "I have taken nothing from any flesh, not even a sandal." And no flesh complained against him.
And after his falling asleep he prophesied. He made his end known to the king, and he raised his voice from the earth in prophecy to blot out the iniquities of his people.
And after him he raised up Nathan to prophesy in the days of David.
As the fat is set apart from the sacrifices of the offerings of forgiveness, so was David among the sons of Israel.
And he behaved among lions as though he lived among young goats.
Did he not kill the giant in his youth and remove the reproach from among the people, when his hands hurled the small stone from the sling and brought down the boasting of Goliath?
For he called upon the Lord Most High, and he gave him strength to strike down the warrior between the two battle lines. He raised up the horn of his people.
Therefore the women glorified him for his tens of thousands and praised him with the songs of the Lord, until he was made worthy to receive the diadem of glory.
For he destroyed his enemies all around him and wiped out the attacking Philistines there, to this day. And he destroyed them together with their [?].

In all his works he gave them confession to the Holy One Most High, the commandment of glory. He praised him with all his heart and loved his Creator, and every day he rose early to praise him with his song.
There he set the singers at the altar of God, who soften the hearts of the people with the sweet sound of the psaltery.
And he gave beauty to the festivals and adorned the seasons until the end with his praise, and to resound [?] at dawn in his sanctuary.
And the Lord took his sins away from him. The Lord raised up his horn forever and gave him the covenant of kingship and the throne of glory in Israel.
After him he raised up his own son, full of all wisdom, and because of him he lived in spaciousness.
Solomon reigned in days of peace, and the Lord gave him peace on every side, so that he might build the house for his name and prepare it as a sanctuary forever.
How wise you became! From your youth you were filled with your knowledge like a river.
And the parables of figures were filled.
And your name reached the distant islands.
Because of the praises of parables and figures, and the interpretations of the scribes, the nations marveled at you.
In the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of Israel, you gathered gold as if it were tin [?], and you multiplied silver as if it were lead.
And you became master over your flesh.
And you defiled your family line, bringing wrath upon your offspring and regret for your folly.
So that your rebellious sovereignty would be split in two.

But God will not abandon his mercy, nor will he let his faithfulness fall short. He will not blot out the descendants of the one who was his support [?], and the offspring of those who loved him will not be destroyed. He left a remnant to Jacob, and to David his own roots.

Solomon rested with his fathers, and after him there remained one of his descendants, Rehoboam, who added to his folly and was found lacking in wisdom. Through his counsel he truly turned his people back, until the rise of the one who was not to be remembered.
Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel astray and showed Israel the way of sin. Their sin grew very great, so that they were removed from their land.
They sought out [?] all their wicked deeds, until vengeance came upon them.
After this the prophet Elijah arose like fire, and his word blazed like a flame.
He brought a famine of bread upon them, and by his zeal he reduced their numbers.
By his word he shut up the rain, and three times he brought down fire.
How glorious you were in your wonders, Elijah! Who now is like you, who could boast like this?
You raised the dead from the earth and from the depths of Hades by the word of the Most High.
You brought kings down to destruction, and honored men from their beds.
Sinai heard the rebuke, and Horeb heard the law of their punishment.
You anointed kings to carry out punishment, and you anointed prophets to succeed you.
You were taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot with horses of fire.
It is written of you that, at the time of reproofs, you would cut short the wrath before it breaks out, turn the hearts of fathers to their children, and restore the tribes of Jacob.
Blessed are those who know you and are adorned with the love of God, so that we too may live by that same life.
Elijah was taken up in the whirlwind of fire, and Elisha was filled with the Holy Spirit. In his days he did not tremble before rulers, and no human being overpowered him.
No word was too great for him, and after his death his body prophesied.
In his life he worked signs and wonders, and in his death his deeds were marvelous.
Hezekiah fortified his city and brought water into it. He cut through the rock with iron and built pools for the water.
In his days Sennacherib came up and sent Rabshakeh. He came, raised his hand against Zion, and boasted loudly in his arrogance.
Then their hearts and hands trembled, and pains like those of a woman giving birth seized them.
They called on the merciful God and stretched out their hands to him. The Holy One quickly heard them and rescued them through Isaiah.
He struck the camp of the Amorites, and his angel from above crushed them.
Hezekiah did what pleased God and held firmly to the ways of his father David, as the prophet Isaiah had commanded him. Isaiah was great and trustworthy in his visions.
In his days the sun went back, and he added years to the king's life.
By that great spirit he saw the end, and he comforted those who mourned in Zion.
And he told them what was to happen, and the hidden counsels, before those wonders had yet come about.
The memory of Josiah is like a wonderful preparation, like the work of a perfumer preparing spices. It is sweet as honey in every mouth, like the music of singers at a time of feasting.
Upon [?] he set himself to his repentance, and he wiped out all idolatry from their midst.
And his heart was set straight toward the Lord, and in the days of the lawless he strengthened the service of holy things.
Except for David, Hezekiah and Josiah, all the others sinned greatly, for the kings of Judea abandoned the law of the Lord,
and they gave their anointing to foreigners and their glory to another nation.
They brought fire and burned the chosen cities of the sanctuary, and they laid waste its roads
because of Jeremiah, for they had mistreated him too. Yet God had appointed this same Jeremiah as a prophet, with power to uproot, to afflict and to destroy, and likewise to build and to plant.
Ezekiel, who saw the vision of glory that was shown to him on the chariots of the cherubim,
for he remembered his enemies with the voice of thunder, and did good and made the ways prosper;
and also of the twelve prophets, to proclaim their powers from their place, for they comforted Jacob and urged them toward faith and virtue.
How shall we glorify Zerubbabel? For he was like the smith of a signet ring on the right hand,
and so also Jeshua son of Jozadak. In their days they built the house and set up the holy temple of the Lord, prepared for glory forever.
And let the memory of the valiant Nehemiah also be in goodness. He raised up our walls, set up our gates and fastened its bolts, and he raised up and rebuilt our ruined towers.
No one was created on earth like Enoch, for he was taken from the earth into heaven.
And no one on earth was as steadfast as Joseph. He led his brothers to strengthen the people, and even his bones were found worthy of being sought out.
Shem and Seth were glorified among people, more than all those created and born of humankind.
Simon son of Onias was the high priest. In his lifetime, in his own days, he built up the house and strengthened the temple,
and through him the foundations of the height were made firm, up to the second raising of the courts of the temple.
In his days the reservoirs for water were built, of the size of the bronze sea, in the pattern of that sea.
He took the people to heart so that they would not fall, and he himself fortified his own city.
How glorious he was as he moved among the people, at the raised part of the court, as he came out of the temple!
He was like the morning star that comes out among the clouds, and like the full moon in the days of its appointed season,
like the sun when it shines on the temple of the Most High, like the glorious bow of the Lord when its brightness reaches the clouds,
Like a rose blossom in the days of the new season, like lilies by the outflow of waters, like a young shoot of Lebanon in the days of [?] (summer?);
like incense on the fire of those who fan it, like a vessel of hammered solid gold, adorned and set with precious carbuncles;
like a beautiful olive tree, full of fruit, like a zelkova tree raised up to the clouds of heaven.
And when he put on his glorious robe and clothed himself in the adornment of complete glory, at the time when he approached the altar of the holy place, he was glorified by the adornment of holiness.

When he received the portions from the hands of his brothers, as he himself stood ready before the altar of sacrifices, they stood around him and surrounded him like young fir shoots on Mount Lebanon, like the trees of [?].
All the sons of Aaron stood in their glory, with the Lord's offering in their hands, before the whole people of Israel.
And there was the complete service, sprinkled on the altar, and the adornment of the offering of the Most High God [?], the Almighty.
When he stretched out his hand to the altar of the weighed-out offerings, when he sprinkled the blood and poured it out at the foundations of the altar as a sweet savor to the Most High King,

then the priests, the sons of Aaron, cried out with a loud voice. With the sound of trumpets of hammered metal they cried out and made the sound heard with a great voice, as a remembrance before the Most High.
At that moment all the people together fell on their faces and worshiped the Lord God.
And they praised the Lord God Most High, and the singers also sang with a louder voice, and with the multitude of the people the sound was made sweet.
And the people prayed to the Lord God Most High, and the prayer was offered before the Merciful One until the end, until the order of the service was completed.
When he came down, he lifted up his hands over the people of Israel to give praise to the Lord with his lips and to glory in his name,
for adornment, to behold the glory of the Most High.
Now praise the Lord, all of you, the worker of wonders throughout the earth, who has exalted our days from the womb and deals with us in his mercy,
so that he may give gladness to our hearts and make peace in our days in Israel, as in the days of old,
so that he may make his mercy sure to us and deliver us in his days.
My soul hates two nations, and the third I have not counted as beloved at all:
the peoples who live on the mountains of Samaria, the Philistines, and the foolish people who live in Shechem.
I, Jesus son of Sirach, son of Eleazar, of Jerusalem, wrote this instruction of wisdom in this book. He poured out wisdom from his heart.
Blessed is the one who occupies himself with these things, and whoever stores them up in his heart will become wise.
And if anyone does these things, he will become very wise in everything, for his places are in the fear of the Lord.
I will give thanks to you, my King, and I will give thanks to your name,
for you have been my refuge and helper, and you have delivered my soul from destruction and from the snare, from the slandering tongue, and from the lips that came against me.

Have mercy on me and deliver me, by the greatness of your mercy, from the roarings that were ready to crush me, from the hands of those who sought my life, and from the many afflictions that surrounded me;
from the sight [?] of fire all around me, and from the midst of a fire that I had not kindled;
from the depth of the abysses of Hades, and from the tongue of foul slander
and from the tongue of the [?] and of slander. Before the king my soul came near to death, and my life drew near to Hades.
They surrounded me, and there was no one to help me. I looked for help from men, and I found none.
I remembered your mercy, O Lord, and the works of your hands from of old, for you deliver those who wait patiently for you, and you rescue them from the hands of the gentiles.
And the Lord lifted my prayers up from the earth, and I prayed to be delivered from death.

And I called upon the Lord, my Father, to the Lord, my Savior: "Do not forsake me, O Lord, in the days of my affliction, in the time of the proud, [when there is no?] help for the weak; and I will praise you with thanksgiving."
Then he heard my voice and delivered me from destruction and rescued me in the evil time.
Therefore I will give thanks to you and praise you, and I will sing to your name for ever and ever, O Lord.
Up to here are the words of Jesus, son of Eleazar, son of Sirach. Before I had gone astray, I openly asked for wisdom in my prayer.
I lay prostrate before the temple and prayed for her, and I sought her to the very end.
As in the time when the grapes ripen and change colour, my foot stood firm and steady, and from my youth I sought her out.
I bent my ear, and I have never been able to draw her out [?]. I found much knowledge in her.
And I prospered. I will give glory to the one who gave me wisdom.
I resolved to live by her, and I was zealous for the good, and I will not be put to shame.
For my soul imitated her, and by my deeds I made her firm. I lifted up my hands on high and reflected on my wisdom.
I directed my soul toward her, I set my mind on her, and in purity I found her.
Therefore my share was not found worn out in her weakness [?]; for her sake I gained the reward of purity.
The Lord gave me a tongue as my reward; with it, praise him.
[Come?] to me, you who are ignorant, and rest in the house of instruction.
What is it that you lack, while your souls are so very thirsty?
I opened my mouth and said: "Now get it for yourselves without money."
"Bend your necks under the yoke and receive instruction, for she is near and can be found."
"See with your own eyes that I labored only a little and found rest."
Acquire knowledge rather than silver, and obtain it rather than gold.
Let your souls rejoice in his mercy, and do not be ashamed of his praise.
Do your good work before the time, and he will give you the unfailing reward in his own time.
